chapters.name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.q: An ideal gas is made of polyatomic molecules. Each of the molecules has three translational, three rotational and \(f\) number of vibrational modes. If the ratio of heat capacities \(C_P/C_V\) of the gas is \(8/7\), then the value of \(f\) is:
questions.sol: Each vibrational mode adds 2 degrees of freedom (kinetic + potential): \(F = 3 + 3 + 2f\). \(\gamma = 1 + \dfrac2F = \dfrac87 \Rightarrow F = 14 \Rightarrow 2f = 8 \Rightarrow f = 4\).

questions.q: One main scale division of a Vernier calliper is equal to 1 mm and the number of divisions on the Vernier scale is 10. When both the jaws touch each other, the Vernier scale shifts to the left of zero of the main scale in such a way that 4th Vernier division coincides with a division of the main scale. If this Vernier calliper measures the length of a wire to be 1 cm, the actual length of the wire is:
questions.sol: Least count \(= \dfrac{1\text{ mm}}{10} = 0.01\) cm. The vernier zero is to the left of the main-scale zero, so the zero error is negative: \(-(10 - 4)\times0.01 = -0.06\) cm. Corrected length \(= 1 - (-0.06) = 1.06\) cm, which is not among the options; NTA dropped the question.
questions.note: NTA dropped this question in the final answer key (all candidates were given full marks).

questions.q: Three identical p-n junction diodes \(D_1\), \(D_2\) and \(D_3\) are connected across a battery as shown in the figure. If the width of the depletion regions of \(D_1\), \(D_2\) and \(D_3\) are \(W_1\), \(W_2\) and \(W_3\), respectively, then the correct option is:
questions.sol: Depletion width depends on bias: forward bias narrows it, reverse bias widens it. \(D_1\) is forward biased, so \(W_1\) is smallest. \(D_3\) faces the other way and is reverse biased, so \(W_3\) is largest. \(D_2\)'s branch is open at one end, so \(D_2\) is unbiased and \(W_2\) lies in between: \(W_3 > W_2 > W_1\).

questions.q: Consider a spring-mass simple harmonic oscillator in one dimension. The mass of the particle is \(m\) kg and the spring constant is \(k\ \text{N m}^{-1}\). At a given instant, the extension of the spring is \(x\) metre and the speed of the particle is \(v\ \text{m s}^{-1}\). On the \(x\)–\(v\) plane, if the graph of \(v\) as a function of \(x\) is a circle, then the correct option is:
questions.sol: Energy: \(\tfrac12mv^2 + \tfrac12kx^2 = E \Rightarrow mv^2 + kx^2 = 2E\). This is a circle in the \(x\)–\(v\) plane only if the two coefficients are equal: \(k = m\) (numerically).

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave travelling in a lossless dielectric medium having a dielectric constant \(\varepsilon_r = 9\), has the electric field \(E_x = E_0\sin(kz - 2\pi\times10^6 t)\ \text{V m}^{-1}\) where \(E_0\) is the amplitude and \(k\) is the wave vector. Among the following options, the incorrect choice is:
o: The wavelength of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium is 300 m
The magnetic field is given by the relation \(B_y = \dfrac{B_0}{v}\sin(kz - 2\pi\times10^6 t)\) where \(v\) is the speed of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium
The direction of propagation of the electromagnetic wave is along \(+z\)
The speed of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium is \(10^8\ \text{m s}^{-1}\)
questions.sol: \(v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_r}} = 10^8\ \text{m s}^{-1}\) and \(f = 10^6\) Hz, so \(\lambda = \dfrac vf = 100\) m: statement (1) is incorrect. \(B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{v}\); statement (2) writes the amplitude as \(\dfrac{B_0}{v}\), which is also incorrect. Propagation along \(+z\) and speed \(10^8\) m/s are correct. NTA accepted both (1) and (2).
questions.note: NTA's final key accepts both (1) and (2).

questions.q: A frictionless circular wire of unit radius is fixed on the horizontal plane. Two point particles of unit mass start moving simultaneously from point A \(\left(\theta = \frac\pi2\right)\) with identical uniform angular speeds in opposite directions, and meet again at point B \(\left(\theta = -\frac\pi2\right)\). During this time, which of the following figures schematically represent the magnitude of the total linear momentum \(P\) of the system, as a function of \(\theta\)?
questions.sol: The particles move symmetrically about the vertical diameter: their horizontal momenta cancel and their vertical momenta add. At A and at B their velocities are horizontal and opposite, so \(P = 0\); halfway (\(\theta = 0\)) both move straight down, so \(P\) is maximum (\(P = 2v\cos\theta\)). The graph is an arch: (2).

questions.q: In Geiger-Marsden experiment, the number of scattered α-particles \(N(\theta)\) is plotted as a function of scattering angle \(\theta\). Which of the following options represents the correct plot?
questions.sol: Rutherford scattering: \(N(\theta) \propto \dfrac{1}{\sin^4(\theta/2)}\). The count is very large at small angles and falls steeply as \(\theta\) increases: graph (2).

questions.q: Consider three media P, Q and R with refractive indices 1, 1.25, and 1.5, respectively. The medium Q having a thickness of 5 cm is placed between extended media P and R as shown in the figure. An object O is placed at the center of medium Q. If viewed from medium P near the normal direction, the apparent depth of O is \(h_1\). For similar observation from medium R, the apparent depth is \(h_2\). The value of \(|h_1 - h_2|\), in cm, is:
questions.sol: O is 2.5 cm inside Q from each face. Apparent depth \(= \text{real depth}\times\dfrac{n_{\text{observer}}}{n_Q}\). From P: \(h_1 = 2.5\times\dfrac{1}{1.25} = 2\) cm. From R: \(h_2 = 2.5\times\dfrac{1.5}{1.25} = 3\) cm. \(|h_1 - h_2| = 1\) cm.

questions.q: Consider that \(\sigma_s\), \(k_B\), \(b\) represent Stefan-Boltzmann constant, Boltzmann constant and Wien's displacement law constant, respectively. The dimension of \(\sigma_s k_B^{-1} b\) is:
questions.sol: \([\sigma_s] = [\text{MT}^{-3}\text{K}^{-4}]\), \([k_B] = [\text{ML}^2\text{T}^{-2}\text{K}^{-1}]\), \([b] = [\text{LK}]\). \(\sigma_s k_B^{-1}b = \dfrac{\text{MT}^{-3}\text{K}^{-4}}{\text{ML}^2\text{T}^{-2}\text{K}^{-1}}\cdot\text{LK} = [\text{L}^{-1}\text{T}^{-1}\text{K}^{-2}]\).

questions.q: For sound waves, if the number of nodes for the 5th harmonic of an open-ended pipe is \(n\) and that for the 9th harmonic of the same pipe with one of its ends closed is \(m\), the ratio \(\dfrac nm\) is:
questions.sol: Open pipe, \(n\)-th harmonic: \(n\) nodes, so the 5th harmonic has 5 nodes. Closed pipe: the 9th harmonic is \((2k - 1) = 9\), i.e. \(k = 5\), with 5 nodes. \(\dfrac nm = 1\).

questions.q: Two infinitely long parallel conducting wires A and B carry currents \(I\) and \(2I\), respectively, in the same direction. The wire A has uniform mass per unit length \(\lambda\) and lies on an insulated floor. The wire B is kept fixed at a height \(h\) above the floor. The minimum magnitude of \(h\) so that the wire A does not rise from the floor is: [\(g\) is the acceleration due to gravity and \(\mu_0\) is the permeability of free space.]
questions.sol: Parallel currents attract, so B pulls A upward with force per length \(\dfrac{\mu_0 I(2I)}{2\pi h} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{\pi h}\). A stays down if this is at most \(\lambda g\): \(h \ge \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{\pi\lambda g}\).

questions.q: An ac voltage \(V = 220\sin(2\times10^3 t)\) volt is applied to a series LCR circuit. Then the current amplitude in this circuit is: (Given: \(L = 10\) mH, \(C = 25\ \mu\text{F}\), \(R = 100\ \Omega\))

Consider a fixed uniformly charged insulating sphere with radius \(R\) and total charge \(+Q\). A point charge \(-q\) (\(q \ll Q\)) with mass \(m\) is released from rest at a distance of \(3R\) from the centre of the charged sphere. When the point charge reaches the surface of the sphere, its speed is: (\(\varepsilon_0\) is the permittivity of vacuum, neglect gravitational forces).
questions.sol: Energy: \(\tfrac12mv^2 = \dfrac{Qq}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\dfrac1R - \dfrac{1}{3R}\right) = \dfrac{Qq}{6\pi\varepsilon_0 R}\). So \(v = \sqrt{\dfrac{Qq}{3\pi\varepsilon_0 mR}}\).

questions.q: A beam of light falls on a metal surface such that photo-electrons are generated. If power of the light source starts to decrease linearly with time \(t\), then variation of the photocurrent \(I\) and magnitude of the stopping potential \(|V|\) with time is best represented by:
questions.sol: Lower power means fewer photons, so the photocurrent falls linearly with time. The frequency is unchanged, so the stopping potential stays constant: graph (4).

questions.q: Two planets \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) with equal mass have radii \(R_1\) and \(R_2\), respectively, where \(R_2 = \dfrac{R_1}{2}\). The escape speeds of \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) are \(v_1\) and \(v_2\), respectively. Then \(\dfrac{v_2}{v_1}\) is:
questions.sol: \(v_e = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt R}\). Halving \(R\): \(\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt2\).

questions.q: A unit positive point charge is taken slowly through an infinitesimally thin tube that is inside a charged dielectric sphere of radius \(R\), having uniform positive charge density \(\rho\), as shown in the figure. The initial and final positions of the charge are marked by A and B at distances \(2R\) and \(3R\) respectively, from the centre of the sphere. In this process, the magnitude of the total work done on the point charge is \(\dfrac{\rho R^2}{n\varepsilon_0}\). The value of \(n\) is: (\(\varepsilon_0\) is the permittivity of vacuum)
questions.sol: A and B are outside the sphere, so the sphere acts like a point charge \(Q = \tfrac43\pi R^3\rho\). Work \(= Q\cdot\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\dfrac{1}{2R} - \dfrac{1}{3R}\right) = \dfrac{\tfrac43\pi R^3\rho}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\cdot\dfrac{1}{6R} = \dfrac{\rho R^2}{18\varepsilon_0}\). So \(n = 18\).

questions.q: One mole of an ideal monatomic gas undergoes a cyclic process as shown in the figure. The total heat supplied to the gas is:
questions.sol: Over a full cycle \(\Delta U = 0\), so heat supplied = net work = area of the loop \(= (5 - 2)\times(300 - 100) = 600\) J (positive, since the cycle runs clockwise).

questions.q:
The following table presents the part of the electromagnetic spectrum and their corresponding major applications.
Part of the electromagnetic spectrumApplications
P. MicrowaveI. For purifying the water
Q. UV raysII. For warming the food
R. Gamma raysIII. For AM and FM communication systems
S. Radio waveIV. For treating the cancer cells
The correct option is:
questions.sol: Microwaves heat food (II), UV rays purify water (I), gamma rays treat cancer (IV), radio waves carry AM/FM (III): P-II, Q-I, R-IV, S-III.

questions.q: A car travels on a circular racetrack of radius 50 m, which is banked at an angle \(\theta\). If the car travels at a speed \(10\ \text{m s}^{-1}\), then the wear and tear on its tyres is minimum. Taking the acceleration due to gravity to be \(10\ \text{m s}^{-2}\), the value of \(\theta\) is:
questions.sol: Least tyre wear means no friction is needed: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{v^2}{rg} = \dfrac{100}{50\times10} = \dfrac15\).

questions.q: Consider a particle moving along a straight line, whose position as a function of time is given by \(s(t) = \alpha t^2 - \beta t + \gamma\), where \(\alpha = 1\ \text{m s}^{-2}\), \(\beta = 6\ \text{m s}^{-1}\) and \(\gamma = 5\) m. The average speed of the particle, in \(\text{m s}^{-1}\), from \(t = 0\) to \(t = 6\) s is:
questions.sol: \(s = t^2 - 6t + 5\), \(v = 2t - 6\): the particle turns at \(t = 3\) s. \(s(0) = 5\), \(s(3) = -4\), \(s(6) = 5\). Distance \(= 9 + 9 = 18\) m in 6 s, so average speed \(= 3\ \text{m s}^{-1}\).

questions.q: A point charge Q is placed inside a cavity within a solid isolated conducting sphere. Consider points A, B and C as shown in the figure, where the magnitudes of the electric fields are \(E_A\), \(E_B\) and \(E_C\), respectively. The points B and C are at the same distance from the center of the solid sphere. The correct option is:
questions.sol: Inside the cavity the field of Q is present, so \(E_A \ne 0\). Charge \(+Q\) spreads uniformly on the outer surface (the conductor shields the cavity), so outside the field is radial and symmetric: \(E_B = E_C\).

questions.q: In the measurement of viscosity of liquids using terminal velocity experiment, spherical balls of same radius but having different densities are used. The variation of the terminal velocity (\(v\)) with the ratio of density of spherical ball (\(\sigma\)) to density of the liquid (\(\rho\)), is best represented by:
questions.sol: Terminal velocity \(v = \dfrac{2r^2g(\sigma - \rho)}{9\eta} \propto \left(\dfrac\sigma\rho - 1\right)\). Its magnitude is zero at \(\sigma/\rho = 1\) and grows linearly on either side (balls lighter than the liquid rise): graph (4).

questions.q: A ray of light with wavelength \(\lambda\) is incident on three different photo-electric cells namely 1, 2 and 3. The threshold wavelength of these photo-electric cells are \(\lambda_1\), \(\lambda_2\), and \(\lambda_3\), respectively and the magnitude of stopping potentials of these cells are \(V_1\), \(V_2\) and \(V_3\), respectively. The relation between \(\lambda\) and threshold wavelengths are \(\lambda_1 < \lambda\), \(\lambda_2 > \lambda\) and \(\lambda_3 \gg \lambda\). The correct option is:
questions.sol: Cell 1: \(\lambda > \lambda_1\), so the photon energy is below the work function and \(V_1 = 0\). Cells 2 and 3 emit, and a larger threshold wavelength means a smaller work function, so the stopping potential is larger: \(V_2 < V_3\).

questions.q: A current \(I_0\) flows through a metallic circular loop of radius \(r\) as shown in the figure. Resistance of the segment ABC is half that of ADC. Magnitude of magnetic field at the center O of the loop is:
questions.sol: The two halves are in parallel: \(I_{ABC} = \tfrac23 I_0\) and \(I_{ADC} = \tfrac13 I_0\). Each semicircle gives \(\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4r}\) at O, in opposite directions: \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4r}\left(\tfrac23 - \tfrac13\right)I_0 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_0}{12r}\).

questions.q: A particle of mass \(M\) moves along a horizontal \(x\) axis from \(x = 0\) to \(x = L\). The coefficient of kinetic friction varies as a function of \(x\) as \(\mu_k(x) = \mu_0 - \alpha x\), where \(\mu_0\), \(\alpha\) are constants of appropriate dimensions, so that \(\mu_k(L) = 0\). The total work done by the frictional force during the motion is \(n\mu_0 MgL\), where \(g\) is the acceleration due to gravity. The value of \(n\) is:
questions.sol: \(\mu_k(L) = 0 \Rightarrow \alpha = \dfrac{\mu_0}{L}\). Work \(= \int_0^L \mu_k Mg\,dx = Mg\left(\mu_0 L - \dfrac{\alpha L^2}{2}\right) = \dfrac12\mu_0 MgL\) in magnitude, so \(n = \dfrac12\).

questions.q: In a solar system, the time-period of revolution of a planet tracing a circular orbit of radius \(R\) is proportional to:
questions.sol: Kepler's third law: \(T^2 \propto R^3 \Rightarrow T \propto R^{3/2}\).

questions.q: A solid sphere A of radius \(R\) and mass \(M\) is attached at a point to a smaller solid sphere B of radius \(r < R\) and mass \(m < M\). Assume that the line joining their centres lies along the horizontal. The moment of inertia of the system calculated about a vertical axis passing through the centre of A is \(I_A\) and that calculated about a vertical axis passing through the centre of B is \(I_B\). The difference \(I_A - I_B\) is:
questions.sol: \(I_A = I_{A,\text{own}} + I_{B,\text{own}} + m(R + r)^2\) and \(I_B = I_{B,\text{own}} + I_{A,\text{own}} + M(R + r)^2\). Difference \(I_A - I_B = (m - M)(R + r)^2\).

questions.q: The lens combination as shown in the figure, consists of two lenses, \(L_1\) and \(L_2\), of the focal lengths +10 cm and −10 cm, respectively. The position of the image formed is:
o: 60 cm to the left of the concave lens
30 cm to the right of the concave lens
60 cm to the right of the concave lens
20 cm to the left of the concave lens
questions.sol: Lens \(L_1\): \(u = -30\), \(f = 10 \Rightarrow v = +15\) cm. This image is 12 cm beyond \(L_2\) (a virtual object). For \(L_2\): \(\dfrac1v = \dfrac{1}{-10} + \dfrac{1}{12} = -\dfrac{1}{60} \Rightarrow v = -60\) cm: 60 cm to the left of the concave lens.

questions.q: An ideal Zener diode with breakdown voltage of −3 V is reverse biased with a negative input voltage \(V_i = -5\) V. The magnitude of voltage difference between points B and A is:
questions.sol: The Zener diode is in breakdown and holds 3 V across itself. The rest of the 5 V appears across the resistor between B and A: \(|V_B - V_A| = 5 - 3 = 2\) V.

questions.q: Three identical capacitors P, Q and S, each of the capacitance \(C\), are connected to a battery of voltage \(V\), as shown in the figure. If the energy stored in the capacitor P and total energy stored in the system are \(U_P\) and \(U_T\), respectively, then the ratio \(\dfrac{U_P}{U_T}\) is:
questions.sol: P and Q in series: \(\dfrac C2\), each with \(\dfrac V2\). S has \(V\). \(U_P = \tfrac12C\left(\dfrac V2\right)^2 = \dfrac{CV^2}{8}\); \(U_T = \tfrac12\cdot\dfrac C2V^2 + \tfrac12CV^2 = \dfrac34CV^2\). Ratio \(= \dfrac16\).

questions.q: A conducting loop of finite resistance lies on the \(x\)–\(y\) plane. There is a constant magnetic field in the \(z\) direction. The area of the loop varies with time \(t\), as \(A = A_0(1 + \sin t)\) in appropriate units. The figure that correctly indicates the qualitative behaviour of the power \(P\) dissipated in the loop as a function of time is:
questions.sol: \(\varepsilon = -B\dfrac{dA}{dt} = -BA_0\cos t\), so \(P = \dfrac{\varepsilon^2}{R} \propto \cos^2 t\). It starts at its maximum, falls to zero at \(t = \tfrac\pi2\) and rises again: graph (1).

questions.q: Consider two circuits, (A) and (B), each having two resistors. One of them has a positive temperature coefficient of resistance, \(+\alpha\), while the other one has a negative temperature of coefficient, \(-\alpha\), as shown in the figure. The current through these circuits are denoted by \(I_A\) and \(I_B\). At initial temperature, the resistance of the two resistors is \(R_0\). As the temperature is increased, the correct option that describes the variation of current in these circuits is:
questions.sol: Circuit A (series): \(R_0(1 - \alpha\Delta T) + R_0(1 + \alpha\Delta T) = 2R_0\), constant, so \(I_A\) is constant. Circuit B (parallel): \(R = \dfrac{R_0(1 - \alpha^2\Delta T^2)}{2}\), which decreases, so \(I_B\) increases.

questions.q: Bob B of mass \(m\) at rest is hanging vertically from the ceiling via a massless string of length 10 m, as shown in the figure. Point mass A of mass \(m\) travelling horizontally with speed \(10\ \text{m s}^{-1}\) hits bob B elastically. The bob B rises \(h\) meter after the collision. Taking the acceleration due to gravity \(g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}\) and neglecting the size of the bob, the value of \(h\) is:
questions.sol: An elastic collision between equal masses exchanges velocities: B moves off at 10 m/s. \(h = \dfrac{v^2}{2g} = \dfrac{100}{20} = 5\) m (less than the 10 m string, so it stays taut).

questions.q: A cylindrical cork of uniform density floats in a liquid of density \(\rho_1\). If the cork is depressed slightly and released, it oscillates harmonically with time period \(T\). If the same cork floats in another liquid of density \(\rho_2\), then the similar oscillation has time period \(2T\). The value of \(\rho_2/\rho_1\) is:
questions.sol: For a floating cylinder \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{\rho Ag}} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt\rho}\). Doubling \(T\) needs \(\rho_2 = \dfrac{\rho_1}{4}\).

questions.q: The mean free path of molecules in an ideal gas A is half that of another ideal gas B. The diameter of the spherical molecules of gas A is twice the diameter of the molecules of B. If number densities of the gases A and B are \(n_A\) and \(n_B\), respectively, then the correct option is:
questions.sol: \(\lambda = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2\,\pi d^2 n}\), so \(nd^2 \propto \dfrac1\lambda\). \(n_A(2d)^2 = 2\,n_Bd^2 \Rightarrow n_A = \dfrac12 n_B\).

questions.q: Consider the following nuclear reaction: \({}^{238}\text{U} \to {}^{234}\text{Th} + {}^4\text{He}\). Take masses of \({}^{238}\text{U}\), \({}^{234}\text{Th}\) and \({}^4\text{He}\) as 238.050 u, 234.043 u and 4.003 u, respectively. The Q value for the reaction, in keV, is: [Given: 1 u = 931.5 MeV c⁻²]
Consider a long solenoid of length \(l\) and radius \(r\). If \(n\) is the number of turns per unit length and \(\mu_0\) is the permeability of free space, the inductance of the solenoid is:
Which of the following measurements require ‘index correction’?
o: Measurement of gravitational acceleration using simple pendulum
Measurement of focal length of lenses using optical bench
Measurement of speed of sound using resonance tube
Measurement of resistance of a wire using meter bridge
questions.sol: On an optical bench the scale distance between the uprights may differ from the true distance between the lens and the needle, so an index correction is applied when measuring focal lengths.

questions.q: The temperature of a metallic sphere of radius \(R\) is increased by a small amount \(\Delta T\). If the linear coefficient of thermal expansion of the metal is \(\alpha\), the approximate increase in the volume of the sphere is:
questions.sol: \(\Delta V = \gamma V\Delta T = 3\alpha\cdot\tfrac43\pi R^3\Delta T = 4\pi R^3\alpha\Delta T\).

questions.q: A photon and an electron, each of 20 eV energy, move in free space. The ratio of linear momentum of electron \(p_e\) to that of photon \(p_{Ph}\), \(\dfrac{p_e}{p_{Ph}}\) is: (Take speed of light \(= 3\times10^8\ \text{m s}^{-1}\), charge of electron \(= -1.6\times10^{-19}\) C and mass of electron \(= 9\times10^{-31}\) kg)
questions.sol: \(p_e = \sqrt{2mE} = \sqrt{2\times9\times10^{-31}\times20\times1.6\times10^{-19}} = 2.4\times10^{-24}\). \(p_{Ph} = \dfrac Ec = \dfrac{3.2\times10^{-18}}{3\times10^8} \approx 1.07\times10^{-26}\). Ratio \(= 225\).

questions.q: Consider that an electron is revolving in an excited state of Hydrogen atom with velocity \(\sqrt{25.6}\times10^5\ \text{m s}^{-1}\). The radius of the orbit is \(x\times10^{-9}\) m. The value of \(x\) is: [Take the mass of electron to be \(9\times10^{-31}\) kg, charge of electron \(= -1.6\times10^{-19}\) C and \(\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9\times10^9\ \text{N m}^2\text{C}^{-2}\)]
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{mv^2}{r} = \dfrac{ke^2}{r^2} \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{ke^2}{mv^2} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times(1.6\times10^{-19})^2}{9\times10^{-31}\times25.6\times10^{10}} = 1\times10^{-9}\) m, so \(x = 1\).

questions.q: Two identical inductors are connected in two different configurations P and Q, where a time varying current \(I(t)\) is flowing, as shown in the figure. The induced emf between points a and b for configuration P is \(E_P\) and that for configuration Q is \(E_Q\). The ratio \(E_P/E_Q\) is: [Neglect the effect of mutual inductance.]
questions.sol: P: a and b are across one inductor carrying \(I\): \(E_P = L\dfrac{dI}{dt}\). Q: a and b are across the parallel pair, each carrying \(\dfrac I2\): \(E_Q = L\dfrac{d(I/2)}{dt}\). \(\dfrac{E_P}{E_Q} = 2\).

questions.q: In an adiabatic expansion, the temperature of one mole of an ideal monatomic gas (\(\gamma = 5/3\)) decreases from 60 K to 50 K. The work done by the gas in the process is: (Take the universal gas constant as \(R = 8.3\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\))

Water flows in a streamline motion through a horizontal pipe of circular cross-section as shown in the figure. The pressure difference of water between P and Q is \(15\ \text{N m}^{-2}\). The area of cross-section at P and Q are 40 cm² and 20 cm², respectively. The rate of flow of water through the pipe, in \(\text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}\), is: [Take density of water \(= 1000\ \text{kg m}^{-3}\)]
questions.sol: Continuity: \(v_Q = 2v_P\). Bernoulli: \(15 = \tfrac12(1000)(4v_P^2 - v_P^2) \Rightarrow v_P = 0.1\) m/s. Flow \(= A_Pv_P = 40\times10^{-4}\times0.1 = 4\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}^3/\text{s} = 400\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}\).

questions.q: A thin horizontal disc is rotating about a vertical axis passing through its fixed centre O. Its angular momentum is \(L_A\) and \(L_B\) computed about points A and B, respectively, with OB = 2 × OA. The value of \(\dfrac{L_A}{L_B}\) is:
questions.sol: The disc's centre is fixed, so its centre-of-mass momentum is zero. The angular momentum about any point is then the same as about O: \(L_A = L_B\), ratio 1.

questions.q: Consider a water tank shown in the figure. It has one wall at \(x = L\) and can be taken to be very wide in the \(z\) direction. When filled with a liquid of surface tension \(S\) and density \(\rho\), the liquid surface makes angle \(\theta_0\) (\(\theta_0 \ll 1\)) with the \(x\)-axis at \(x = L\). If \(y(x)\) is the height of the surface then the equation for \(y(x)\) is: (take \(\theta(x) \approx \sin\theta(x) \approx \tan\theta(x) = \frac{dy}{dx}\), \(g\) is the acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol: Across the curved surface, surface tension gives a pressure difference \(S\,\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\) (small slope, so curvature \(\approx y''\)). It must balance the hydrostatic pressure \(\rho g y\) at height \(y\): \(S\,y'' = \rho g y \Rightarrow \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{\rho g}{S}\,y\).

questions.q: A microscope has an objective of focal length 2 cm, eyepiece of focal length 4 cm and the tube length of 40 cm. If the distance of distinct vision of eye is 25 cm, the magnification in the microscope is
questions.sol: Magnification of a compound microscope (final image at \(D\)): \(m = \dfrac{L}{f_o}\cdot\dfrac{D}{f_e} = \dfrac{40}{2}\times\dfrac{25}{4} = 20 \times 6.25 = 125\).

questions.q: An electron (mass \(9 \times 10^{-31}\) kg and charge \(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\) C) moving with speed \(c/100\) (\(c\) = speed of light) is injected into a magnetic field \(\vec B\) of magnitude \(9 \times 10^{-4}\) T perpendicular to its direction of motion. We wish to apply a uniform electric field \(\vec E\) together with the magnetic field so that the electron does not deflect from its path. Then (speed of light \(c = 3 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}\))
o: \(\vec E\) is perpendicular to \(\vec B\) and its magnitude is \(27 \times 10^{4}\ \text{V m}^{-1}\)
\(\vec E\) is perpendicular to \(\vec B\) and its magnitude is \(27 \times 10^{2}\ \text{V m}^{-1}\)
\(\vec E\) is parallel to \(\vec B\) and its magnitude is \(27 \times 10^{2}\ \text{V m}^{-1}\)
\(\vec E\) is parallel to \(\vec B\) and its magnitude is \(27 \times 10^{4}\ \text{V m}^{-1}\)
questions.sol: No deflection when \(qE = qvB\), with \(\vec E\) perpendicular to both \(\vec v\) and \(\vec B\). \(E = vB = (3\times10^{6})(9\times10^{-4}) = 2700 = 27\times10^{2}\ \text{V m}^{-1}\).

questions.q: There are two inclined surfaces of equal length (\(L\)) and same angle of inclination \(45^\circ\) with the horizontal. One of them is rough and the other is perfectly smooth. A given body takes 2 times as much time to slide down on the rough surface than on the smooth surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction (\(\mu_k\)) between the object and the rough surface is close to
questions.sol: Smooth: \(L = \tfrac12 g\sin45^\circ\,t^2\). Rough: \(L = \tfrac12 g(\sin45^\circ - \mu\cos45^\circ)(2t)^2\). Equating: \(\sin45^\circ = 4(\sin45^\circ - \mu\cos45^\circ) \Rightarrow 1 = 4(1-\mu) \Rightarrow \mu = \tfrac34 = 0.75\).

questions.q: The kinetic energies of two similar cars A and B are 100 J and 225 J respectively. On applying brakes, car A stops after 1000 m and car B stops after 1500 m. If \(F_A\) and \(F_B\) are the forces applied by the brakes on cars A and B, respectively, then the ratio \(F_A/F_B\) is
questions.sol: Work done by the brakes = kinetic energy, so \(F = \dfrac{K}{s}\). \(F_A = \dfrac{100}{1000} = 0.1\) N, \(F_B = \dfrac{225}{1500} = 0.15\) N, so \(\dfrac{F_A}{F_B} = \dfrac{2}{3}\).

questions.q: The current passing through the battery in the given circuit is:
questions.sol: Between B and E there is a Wheatstone bridge: \(\dfrac{R_{BA}}{R_{AE}} = \dfrac{5}{3}\) and \(\dfrac{R_{BD}}{R_{DE}} = \dfrac{2.5}{1.5} = \dfrac53\). It is balanced, so the 6 Ω arm carries no current. \(R_{BE} = (5+3)\,\|\,(2.5+1.5) = 8\,\|\,4 = \dfrac83\) Ω. Total \(= \dfrac83 + 1.5 + 5.5 + \dfrac13 = 10\) Ω, so \(I = \dfrac{5}{10} = 0.5\) A.

questions.q: A bob of heavy mass \(m\) is suspended by a light string of length \(l\). The bob is given a horizontal velocity \(v_0\) as shown in figure. If the string gets slack at some point P making an angle \(\theta\) from the horizontal, the ratio of the speed \(v\) of the bob at point P to its initial speed \(v_0\) is:
questions.sol: String slack at P: tension zero, so \(mg\sin\theta = \dfrac{mv^2}{l} \Rightarrow v^2 = gl\sin\theta\). P is \(l(1+\sin\theta)\) above the start: \(v_0^2 = v^2 + 2gl(1+\sin\theta) = gl(2 + 3\sin\theta)\). Hence \(\dfrac{v}{v_0} = \left(\dfrac{\sin\theta}{2+3\sin\theta}\right)^{1/2}\).

questions.q: The output (Y) of the given logic implementation is similar to the output of an/a ______ gate.
questions.sol: Top gate: NOR \(\Rightarrow \overline{A+B}\). Bottom gate: NAND \(\Rightarrow \overline{AB}\). Output \(Y = \overline{A+B}\cdot\overline{AB} = \bar A\bar B\,(\bar A + \bar B) = \bar A\bar B = \overline{A+B}\): a NOR gate.

questions.q: The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by \(E_z = 60\cos(5x + 1.5 \times 10^{9} t)\ \text{V/m}\). Then the expression for the corresponding magnetic field is (here subscripts denote the direction of the field):
questions.sol: \(B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{c} = \dfrac{60}{3\times10^8} = 2\times10^{-7}\) T. The phase \(5x + \omega t\) means the wave moves along \(-x\). \(\vec E\times\vec B\) must point along \(-\hat x\): \(\hat z \times \hat y = -\hat x\), so \(\vec B\) is along \(y\): \(B_y = 2\times10^{-7}\cos(5x + 1.5\times10^9 t)\) T.

questions.q: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from a height of 40 m. The ball hits the ground and rises to a height of 10 m. The impulse imparted to the ball during its collision with the ground is (Take \(g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2\))
questions.sol: Speed on hitting: \(\sqrt{2\times9.8\times40} = 28\) m/s (down). Speed after: \(\sqrt{2\times9.8\times10} = 14\) m/s (up). Impulse \(= m(v_2 + v_1) = 0.5\times(14 + 28) = 21\) N s.

questions.q: AB is a part of an electrical circuit (see figure). The potential difference \(V_A - V_B\), at the instant when current \(i = 2\) A and is increasing at a rate of 1 amp/second is:
questions.sol: Going from A to B: drop across the inductor \(L\dfrac{di}{dt} = 1\times1 = 1\) V, across the cell 5 V, across the resistor \(iR = 2\times2 = 4\) V. \(V_A - V_B = 1 + 5 + 4 = 10\) V.

questions.q: A 2 amp current is flowing through two different small circular copper coils having radii ratio 1 : 2. The ratio of their respective magnetic moments will be
questions.sol: \(m = I\pi r^2\), so with the same current \(m \propto r^2\): \(m_1 : m_2 = 1^2 : 2^2 = 1 : 4\).

questions.q: In a certain camera, a combination of four similar thin convex lenses are arranged axially in contact. Then the power of the combination and the total magnification in comparison to the power (\(p\)) and magnification (\(m\)) for each lens will be, respectively
questions.sol: Thin lenses in contact: powers add, \(P = 4p\). The image of each lens is the object of the next, so magnifications multiply: \(m_{\text{total}} = m^4\).

questions.q: An oxygen cylinder of volume 30 litre has 18.20 moles of oxygen. After some oxygen is withdrawn from the cylinder, its gauge pressure drops to 11 atmospheric pressure at temperature \(27^\circ\)C. The mass of the oxygen withdrawn from the cylinder is nearly equal to: [Given, \(R = \frac{100}{12}\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\), and molecular mass of \(\text{O}_2\) = 32, 1 atm pressure \(= 1.01 \times 10^{5}\ \text{N/m}^2\)]
questions.sol: Absolute pressure after = 11 + 1 = 12 atm. Moles left \(n = \dfrac{PV}{RT} = \dfrac{12\times1.01\times10^5\times0.030}{(100/12)\times300} \approx 14.54\). Moles withdrawn \(= 18.20 - 14.54 = 3.66\); mass \(= 3.66\times32 \approx 117\) g \(\approx 0.116\) kg.

questions.q: In some appropriate units, time (\(t\)) and position (\(x\)) relation of a moving particle is given by \(t = x^2 + x\). The acceleration of the particle is
questions.sol: \(t = x^2 + x \Rightarrow \dfrac{dt}{dx} = 2x + 1\), so \(v = \dfrac{1}{2x+1}\). \(a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2x+1}\cdot\dfrac{-2}{(2x+1)^2} = -\dfrac{2}{(2x+1)^3}\).

questions.q: To an ac power supply of 220 V at 50 Hz, a resistor of 20 Ω, a capacitor of reactance 25 Ω and an inductor of reactance 45 Ω are connected in series. The corresponding current in the circuit and the phase angle between the current and the voltage is, respectively:
questions.sol: \(X_L - X_C = 45 - 25 = 20\) Ω, \(Z = \sqrt{20^2 + 20^2} = 20\sqrt2 \approx 28.3\) Ω. \(I = \dfrac{220}{28.3} \approx 7.8\) A; \(\tan\phi = \dfrac{20}{20} = 1 \Rightarrow \phi = 45^\circ\).

questions.q: The Sun rotates around its centre once in 27 days. What will be the period of revolution if the Sun were to expand to twice its present radius without any external influence? Assume the Sun to be a sphere of uniform density.
questions.sol: No external torque, so \(I\omega\) is constant. For a uniform sphere \(I = \tfrac25 MR^2\), so \(T \propto R^2\). Doubling \(R\): \(T = 27\times4 = 108\) days.

questions.q: A model for quantized motion of an electron in a uniform magnetic field \(B\) states that the flux passing through the orbit of the electron is \(n(h/e)\) where \(n\) is an integer, \(h\) is Planck's constant and \(e\) is the magnitude of electron's charge. According to the model, the magnetic moment of an electron in its lowest energy state will be (\(m\) is the mass of the electron)
questions.sol: Lowest state: \(B\pi r^2 = \dfrac{h}{e} \Rightarrow \pi r^2 = \dfrac{h}{eB}\). Orbital current \(I = \dfrac{e}{T} = \dfrac{e^2B}{2\pi m}\). Magnetic moment \(\mu = I\pi r^2 = \dfrac{e^2B}{2\pi m}\cdot\dfrac{h}{eB} = \dfrac{he}{2\pi m}\).

questions.q: Three identical heat conducting rods are connected in series as shown in the figure. The rods on the sides have thermal conductivity \(2K\) while that in the middle has thermal conductivity \(K\). The left end of the combination is maintained at temperature \(3T\) and the right end at \(T\). The rods are thermally insulated from outside. In steady state, temperature at the left junction is \(T_1\) and that at the right junction is \(T_2\). The ratio \(T_1/T_2\) is:
questions.sol: Thermal resistance \(\propto \dfrac{1}{K}\): the outer rods have \(r/2\) each, the middle rod \(r\); total \(2r\). Heat current \(H = \dfrac{3T - T}{2r} = \dfrac{T}{r}\). \(T_1 = 3T - H\dfrac r2 = 2.5T\), \(T_2 = T + H\dfrac r2 = 1.5T\). \(\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \dfrac53\).

questions.q: The plates of a parallel plate capacitor are separated by \(d\). Two slabs of different dielectric constant \(K_1\) and \(K_2\) with thickness \(\frac{3}{8}d\) and \(\frac{d}{2}\), respectively are inserted in the capacitor. Due to this, the capacitance becomes two times larger than when there is nothing between the plates. If \(K_1 = 1.25\,K_2\), the value of \(K_1\) is:
questions.sol: With slabs: \(C' = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d - \frac38 d - \frac d2 + \frac{3d}{8K_1} + \frac{d}{2K_2}} = 2C\). So \(\dfrac d8 + \dfrac{3d}{8K_1} + \dfrac{d}{2K_2} = \dfrac d2\). With \(K_2 = \dfrac{K_1}{1.25} = 0.8K_1\): \(\dfrac{0.375}{K_1} + \dfrac{0.625}{K_1} = \dfrac38 \Rightarrow K_1 = \dfrac83 \approx 2.66\).

questions.q: Two cities X and Y are connected by a regular bus service with a bus leaving in either direction every \(T\) min. A girl is driving scooty with a speed of 60 km/h in the direction X to Y and notices that a bus goes past her every 30 minutes in the direction of her motion, and every 10 minutes in the opposite direction. Choose the correct option for the period \(T\) of the bus service and the speed (assumed constant) of the buses.
questions.sol: Buses in one direction are spaced \(d = v_bT\) apart. Overtaking her: \(\dfrac{d}{v_b - 60} = \dfrac12\) h. Coming towards her: \(\dfrac{d}{v_b + 60} = \dfrac16\) h. Dividing: \(\dfrac{v_b + 60}{v_b - 60} = 3 \Rightarrow v_b = 120\) km/h, \(d = 30\) km, \(T = \dfrac{30}{120}\) h = 15 min.

questions.q: A uniform rod of mass 20 kg and length 5 m leans against a smooth vertical wall making an angle of \(60^\circ\) with it. The other end rests on a rough horizontal floor. The friction force that the floor exerts on the rod is: (take \(g = 10\ \text{m/s}^2\))
questions.sol: Friction \(f\) balances the wall's normal force \(N\). Torques about the foot (rod at \(60^\circ\) to the wall): \(mg\dfrac L2\sin60^\circ = N L\cos60^\circ \Rightarrow f = N = \dfrac{mg}{2}\tan60^\circ = 100\sqrt3\) N.

questions.q: In an oscillating spring mass system, a spring is connected to a box filled with sand. As the box oscillates, sand leaks slowly out of the box vertically so that the average frequency \(\omega(t)\) and average amplitude \(A(t)\) of the system change with time \(t\). Which one of the following options schematically depicts these changes correctly?
questions.sol: \(\omega = \sqrt{k/m}\) increases as mass \(m\) decreases. Sand leaving the moving box carries away kinetic energy, so the energy \(\tfrac12 kA^2\) of the oscillator falls and the amplitude decreases. Option (2): \(\omega\) rises, \(A\) falls.

questions.q: A balloon is made of a material of surface tension \(S\) and its inflation outlet (from where gas is filled in it) has small area \(A\). It is filled with a gas of density \(\rho\) and takes a spherical shape of radius \(R\). When the gas is allowed to flow freely out of it, its radius \(r\) changes from \(R\) to 0 (zero) in time \(T\). If the speed \(v(r)\) of gas coming out of the balloon depends on \(r\) as \(r^a\) and \(T \propto S^\alpha A^\beta \rho^\gamma R^\delta\), then
questions.sol: Excess pressure \(\propto \dfrac Sr\), so \(\tfrac12\rho v^2 \propto \dfrac{S}{r} \Rightarrow v \propto \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{\rho r}}\), i.e. \(a = -\tfrac12\). Volume flow: \(4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -Av \Rightarrow dt \propto \dfrac{r^{5/2}}{A}\sqrt{\dfrac\rho S}\,dr\). Integrating, \(T \propto S^{-1/2}A^{-1}\rho^{1/2}R^{7/2}\).

questions.q: Consider the diameter of a spherical object being measured with the help of a Vernier callipers. Suppose its 10 Vernier Scale Divisions (V.S.D.) are equal to its 9 Main Scale Divisions (M.S.D.). The least division in the M.S. is 0.1 cm and the zero of V.S. is at \(x = 0.1\) cm when the jaws of Vernier callipers are closed. If the main scale reading for the diameter is \(M = 5\) cm and the number of coinciding vernier division is 8, the measured diameter after zero error correction, is:
questions.sol: Least count \(= 1\ \text{MSD} - 1\ \text{VSD} = 0.1 - 0.09 = 0.01\) cm. Reading \(= 5 + 8\times0.01 = 5.08\) cm. Zero error \(= +0.1\) cm, so corrected diameter \(= 5.08 - 0.1 = 4.98\) cm.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor made of circular plates is being charged such that the surface charge density on its plates is increasing at a constant rate with time. The magnetic field arising due to displacement current is:
o: constant between the plates and zero outside the plates
non-zero everywhere with maximum at the imaginary cylindrical surface connecting peripheries of the plates
zero between the plates and non-zero outside
questions.sol: The displacement current is spread uniformly over the plates, so (like a wire with uniform current) \(B \propto r\) inside the plate radius and \(B \propto \dfrac1r\) outside. \(B\) is non-zero everywhere and largest at the edge, \(r = R\).

questions.q: An unpolarized light beam travelling in air is incident on a medium of refractive index 1.73 at Brewster's angle. Then
o: reflected light is completely polarized and the angle of reflection is close to \(60^\circ\)
reflected light is partially polarized and the angle of reflection is close to \(30^\circ\)
both reflected and transmitted light are perfectly polarized with angles of reflection and refraction close to \(60^\circ\) and \(30^\circ\), respectively
transmitted light is completely polarized with angle of refraction close to \(30^\circ\)
questions.sol: At Brewster's angle \(\tan i_B = \mu = 1.73 \Rightarrow i_B = 60^\circ\). The reflected light is completely polarized; angle of reflection = angle of incidence \(= 60^\circ\). (The refracted light is only partly polarized.)

questions.q: Two identical charged conducting spheres A and B have their centres separated by a certain distance. Charge on each sphere is \(q\) and the force of repulsion between them is \(F\). A third identical uncharged conducting sphere is brought in contact with sphere A first and then with B and finally removed from both. New force of repulsion between spheres A and B (radii of A and B are negligible compared to the distance of separation so that for calculating force between them they can be considered as point charges) is best given as:
questions.sol: After touching A: A has \(\dfrac q2\). Third sphere (\(\dfrac q2\)) then touches B: each gets \(\dfrac{q + q/2}{2} = \dfrac{3q}{4}\). New force \(\propto \dfrac q2\cdot\dfrac{3q}{4} = \dfrac38 q^2\), so \(F' = \dfrac{3F}{8}\).

questions.q: A container has two chambers of volumes \(V_1 = 2\) litres and \(V_2 = 3\) litres separated by a partition made of a thermal insulator. The chambers contain \(n_1 = 5\) and \(n_2 = 4\) moles of ideal gas at pressures \(p_1 = 1\) atm and \(p_2 = 2\) atm, respectively. When the partition is removed, the mixture attains an equilibrium pressure of:
questions.sol: Total internal energy is conserved, so \(\sum pV\) is unchanged: \(p(V_1 + V_2) = p_1V_1 + p_2V_2 \Rightarrow p = \dfrac{1\times2 + 2\times3}{5} = 1.6\) atm.

questions.q: A particle of mass \(m\) is moving around the origin with a constant force \(F\) pulling it towards the origin. If Bohr model is used to describe its motion, the radius \(r\) of the \(n^{\text{th}}\) orbit and the particle's speed \(v\) in the orbit depend on \(n\) as
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{mv^2}{r} = F\) and \(mvr = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}\). From the first, \(v \propto r^{1/2}\); then \(r^{3/2} \propto n\), so \(r \propto n^{2/3}\) and \(v \propto r^{1/2} \propto n^{1/3}\).

questions.q: The radius of Martian orbit around the Sun is about 4 times the radius of the orbit of Mercury. The Martian year is 687 Earth days. Then which of the following is the length of 1 year on Mercury?
questions.sol: Kepler's third law: \(T^2 \propto r^3\). \(\dfrac{T_{\text{Mars}}}{T_{\text{Mercury}}} = 4^{3/2} = 8\), so \(T_{\text{Mercury}} = \dfrac{687}{8} \approx 86 \approx 88\) earth days.

questions.q: A body weighs 48 N on the surface of the earth. The gravitational force experienced by the body due to the earth at a height equal to one-third the radius of the earth from its surface is:

A wire of resistance \(R\) is cut into 8 equal pieces. From these pieces two equivalent resistances are made by adding four of these together in parallel. Then these two sets are added in series. The net effective resistance of the combination is:
questions.sol: Each piece is \(\dfrac R8\). Four in parallel: \(\dfrac{R/8}{4} = \dfrac{R}{32}\). Two such sets in series: \(\dfrac{R}{16}\).

questions.q: De-Broglie wavelength of an electron orbiting in the \(n = 2\) state of hydrogen atom is close to (Given Bohr radius = 0.052 nm)
questions.sol: \(r_2 = 2^2 \times 0.052 = 0.208\) nm. Bohr's condition \(2\pi r_n = n\lambda\): \(\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi\times0.208}{2} \approx 0.65\) nm \(\approx 0.67\) nm.

questions.q: An electric dipole with dipole moment \(5 \times 10^{-6}\) C m is aligned with the direction of a uniform electric field of magnitude \(4 \times 10^{5}\) N/C. The dipole is then rotated through an angle of \(60^\circ\) with respect to the electric field. The change in the potential energy of the dipole is:
questions.sol: \(U = -pE\cos\theta\). \(\Delta U = pE(1 - \cos60^\circ) = 5\times10^{-6}\times4\times10^5\times\tfrac12 = 1.0\) J.

questions.q: A constant voltage of 50 V is maintained between the points A and B of the circuit shown in the figure. The current through the branch CD of the circuit is:
questions.sol: Treat C and D as joined by branch CD. Then 1 Ω ∥ 3 Ω \(= 0.75\) Ω and 2 Ω ∥ 4 Ω \(= \tfrac43\) Ω in series: \(R = \tfrac{25}{12}\) Ω and \(I = 24\) A. \(V_{AC} = 24\times0.75 = 18\) V, so 18 A flows in the 1 Ω arm and 6 A in the 3 Ω arm. \(V_{CB} = 32\) V, so 16 A flows in the 2 Ω arm. Current in CD \(= 18 - 16 = 2.0\) A.

questions.q: A photon and an electron (mass \(m\)) have the same energy \(E\). The ratio \((\lambda_{\text{photon}}/\lambda_{\text{electron}})\) of their de Broglie wavelengths is (\(c\) is the speed of light)
questions.sol: Photon: \(\lambda_p = \dfrac{hc}{E}\). Electron: \(\lambda_e = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}\). Ratio \(\dfrac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_e} = \dfrac{c\sqrt{2mE}}{E} = c\sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{E}}\).

questions.q: Which of the following options represent the variation of photoelectric current with property of light shown on the x-axis?
questions.sol: Photocurrent is proportional to intensity, a straight line through the origin, so A is correct and B is wrong. The saturation photocurrent does not depend on frequency (above threshold), so C and D are wrong. Only A.

questions.q: A sphere of radius \(R\) is cut from a larger solid sphere of radius \(2R\) as shown in the figure. The ratio of the moment of inertia of the smaller sphere to that of the rest part of the sphere about the Y-axis is:
questions.sol: Mass of the big sphere \(M\); the cut sphere has \(\dfrac M8\). \(I_{\text{big}} = \tfrac25M(2R)^2 = \tfrac85MR^2\). Cut sphere about Y (parallel axis, distance \(R\)): \(\tfrac25\cdot\tfrac M8R^2 + \tfrac M8R^2 = \tfrac{7}{40}MR^2\). Remainder: \(\tfrac{64}{40} - \tfrac{7}{40} = \tfrac{57}{40}MR^2\). Ratio \(= \dfrac{7}{57}\).

questions.q: A full wave rectifier circuit with diodes (\(D_1\)) and (\(D_2\)) is shown in the figure. If input supply voltage \(V_{in} = 220\sin(100\pi t)\) volt, then at \(t = 15\) ms
o: \(D_1\) is forward biased, \(D_2\) is reverse biased
\(D_1\) is reverse biased, \(D_2\) is forward biased
questions.sol: At \(t = 15\) ms, \(100\pi t = 1.5\pi\), so \(\sin(1.5\pi) = -1\): the negative half cycle. The polarity of the secondary reverses, so \(D_1\) is reverse biased and \(D_2\) conducts.

questions.q: Two gases A and B are filled at the same pressure in separate cylinders with movable pistons of radius \(r_A\) and \(r_B\), respectively. On supplying an equal amount of heat to both the systems reversibly under constant pressure, the pistons of gas A and B are displaced by 16 cm and 9 cm, respectively. If the change in their internal energy is the same, then the ratio \(r_A/r_B\) is equal to
questions.sol: Same heat \(Q\) and same \(\Delta U\) means the same work \(W = p\,\Delta V = p\,\pi r^2 x\). So \(r_A^2\times16 = r_B^2\times9 \Rightarrow \dfrac{r_A}{r_B} = \dfrac34\).

questions.q: A physical quantity \(P\) is related to four observations \(a, b, c\) and \(d\) as follows: \(P = a^3 b^2 / c\sqrt{d}\). The percentage errors of measurement in \(a, b, c\) and \(d\) are 1%, 3%, 2% and 4% respectively. The percentage error in the quantity \(P\) is
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{\Delta P}{P} = 3\dfrac{\Delta a}{a} + 2\dfrac{\Delta b}{b} + \dfrac{\Delta c}{c} + \tfrac12\dfrac{\Delta d}{d} = 3(1) + 2(3) + 2 + \tfrac12(4) = 13\%\).

questions.q: The intensity of transmitted light when a polaroid sheet, placed between two crossed polarizers at \(22.5^\circ\) from the polarization axis of one of the polaroids, is (\(I_0\) is the intensity of polarised light after passing through the first polaroid):
questions.sol: Malus's law twice: \(I = I_0\cos^2 22.5^\circ\cos^2 67.5^\circ = I_0(\cos22.5^\circ\sin22.5^\circ)^2 = I_0\dfrac{\sin^2 45^\circ}{4} = \dfrac{I_0}{8}\).

questions.q: Two identical point masses P and Q, suspended from two separate massless springs of spring constants \(k_1\) and \(k_2\) respectively, oscillate vertically. If their maximum speeds are the same, the ratio \((A_Q/A_P)\) of the amplitude \(A_Q\) of mass Q to the amplitude \(A_P\) of mass P is:
questions.sol: \(v_{\max} = A\omega\) is the same for both, so \(\dfrac{A_Q}{A_P} = \dfrac{\omega_P}{\omega_Q} = \sqrt{\dfrac{k_1/m}{k_2/m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{k_1}{k_2}}\).

questions.q: A pipe open at both ends has a fundamental frequency \(f\) in air. The pipe is now dipped vertically in a water drum to half of its length. The fundamental frequency of the air column is now equal to:
questions.sol: Open pipe: \(f = \dfrac{v}{2L}\). Dipped halfway, it becomes a closed pipe of length \(\dfrac L2\): \(f' = \dfrac{v}{4(L/2)} = \dfrac{v}{2L} = f\).

questions.q: A tightly wound 100 turns coil of radius 10 cm carries a current of 7 A. The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil is (Take permeability of free space as \(4\pi \times 10^{-7}\) SI units):
questions.sol: \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N I}{2r} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times100\times7}{2\times0.1} \approx 4.4\times10^{-3}\) T = 4.4 mT.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Material)List-II (Susceptibility \(\chi\))
(A) Diamagnetic(I) \(\chi = 0\)
(B) Ferromagnetic(II) \(0 > \chi \ge -1\)
(C) Paramagnetic(III) \(\chi \gg 1\)
(D) Non-magnetic(IV) \(0 < \chi < \varepsilon\) (a small positive number)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Diamagnetic: small negative (\(0 > \chi \ge -1\)) → II. Ferromagnetic: \(\chi \gg 1\) → III. Paramagnetic: small positive → IV. Non-magnetic: \(\chi = 0\) → I.

questions.q: A thermodynamic system is taken through the cycle abcda. The work done by the gas along the path bc is:
questions.sol: Path bc is vertical on the P–V graph (volume constant at 400 cm³), so \(W = \int p\,dV = 0\).

questions.q: An unpolarised light beam strikes a glass surface at Brewster's angle. Then
o: both the reflected and refracted light will be completely polarised.
the reflected light will be completely polarised but the refracted light will be partially polarised.
the reflected light will be partially polarised.
the refracted light will be completely polarised.
questions.sol: At Brewster's angle the reflected light is completely plane polarised, while the refracted light is only partially polarised.

questions.q: In an ideal transformer, the turns ratio is \(\dfrac{N_p}{N_s} = \dfrac{1}{2}\). The ratio \(V_s : V_p\) is equal to (the symbols carry their usual meaning):
questions.sol: For an ideal transformer \(\dfrac{V_s}{V_p} = \dfrac{N_s}{N_p} = 2\), so \(V_s : V_p = 2 : 1\).

questions.q:
A logic circuit provides the output \(Y\) as per the following truth table:
ABY
001
010
101
110
questions.sol: \(Y = 1\) exactly when \(B = 0\), whatever \(A\) is. So \(Y = \bar B\).

questions.q: In a vernier calipers, \((N + 1)\) divisions of vernier scale coincide with \(N\) divisions of main scale. If 1 MSD represents 0.1 mm, the vernier constant (in cm) is:
questions.sol: \((N+1)\) VSD \(= N\) MSD, so 1 VSD \(= \dfrac{N}{N+1}\) MSD. Vernier constant \(= 1\text{ MSD} - 1\text{ VSD} = \dfrac{0.1\text{ mm}}{N+1} = \dfrac{0.01}{N+1}\text{ cm} = \dfrac{1}{100(N+1)}\) cm.

questions.q: The maximum elongation of a steel wire of 1 m length if the elastic limit of steel and its Young's modulus, respectively, are \(8 \times 10^{8}\ \text{N m}^{-2}\) and \(2 \times 10^{11}\ \text{N m}^{-2}\), is:
questions.sol: Largest strain \(= \dfrac{\text{elastic limit}}{Y} = \dfrac{8\times10^8}{2\times10^{11}} = 4\times10^{-3}\). Elongation \(= 4\times10^{-3}\times1\text{ m} = 4\) mm.

questions.q: A horizontal force 10 N is applied to a block A as shown in figure. The masses of blocks A and B are 2 kg and 3 kg, respectively. The blocks slide over a frictionless surface. The force exerted by block A on block B is:
questions.sol: Common acceleration \(a = \dfrac{10}{2+3} = 2\ \text{m/s}^2\). Force on B \(= m_Ba = 3\times2 = 6\) N.

questions.q: If the monochromatic source in Young's double slit experiment is replaced by white light, then
o: there will be a central bright white fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes.
all bright fringes will be of equal width.
there will be a central dark fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes.
questions.sol: At the centre the path difference is zero for every wavelength, so all colours add up to a white central fringe. Away from the centre, different wavelengths have different fringe widths, so only a few coloured fringes are seen.

questions.q: The graph which shows the variation of \(\left(\dfrac{1}{\lambda^2}\right)\) and its kinetic energy, \(E\) is (where \(\lambda\) is de Broglie wavelength of a free particle):
questions.sol: \(\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\lambda^2} = \dfrac{2m}{h^2}E\): a straight line through the origin.

questions.q: In the following circuit, the equivalent capacitance between terminal A and terminal B is:
questions.sol: The circuit is symmetric, so both ends of the middle capacitor are at the same potential and it holds no charge. Each branch is 2 μF in series with 2 μF = 1 μF; the two branches in parallel give 2 μF.

questions.q: In the above diagram, a strong bar magnet is moving towards solenoid-2 from solenoid-1. The direction of induced current in solenoid-1 and that in solenoid-2, respectively, are through the directions:
questions.sol: Lenz's law. The S pole approaches solenoid-2, so its near (left) face must become an S pole: current flows from D to C. The N pole moves away from solenoid-1, so its near (right) face must become an S pole to attract it: current flows from A to B.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements A and B and identify the correct answer:
A. For a solar-cell, the I-V characteristics lies in the IV quadrant of the given graph.
B. In a reverse biased pn junction diode, the current measured in (μA), is due to majority charge carriers.
o: Both A and B are correct.
Both A and B are incorrect.
A is correct but B is incorrect.
A is incorrect but B is correct.
questions.sol: A solar cell supplies power, so its I–V curve lies in the fourth quadrant: A is correct. The small reverse current of a p-n diode is due to minority carriers, not majority carriers: B is incorrect.

questions.q: A light ray enters through a right angled prism at point P with the angle of incidence \(30^\circ\) as shown in figure. It travels through the prism parallel to its base BC and emerges along the face AC. The refractive index of the prism is:
questions.sol: At P: \(\sin30^\circ = \mu\sin r_1\). The ray grazes out of AC, so \(r_2 = C\) with \(\sin C = \dfrac1\mu\). With \(A = 90^\circ\): \(r_1 = 90^\circ - C\), so \(\sin r_1 = \cos C = \sqrt{1 - 1/\mu^2}\). Then \(\tfrac12 = \sqrt{\mu^2 - 1} \Rightarrow \mu = \dfrac{\sqrt5}{2}\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: The potential (\(V\)) at any axial point, at 2 m distance (\(r\)) from the centre of the dipole of dipole moment vector \(\vec P\) of magnitude \(4 \times 10^{-6}\) C m, is \(\pm 9 \times 10^{3}\) V. (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^{9}\) SI units)
Reason R: \(V = \pm \dfrac{2P}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}\), where \(r\) is the distance of any axial point, situated at 2 m from the centre of the dipole.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
questions.sol: On the axis \(V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{p}{r^2} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times4\times10^{-6}}{4} = 9\times10^3\) V, so A is true. The factor 2 in R belongs to the axial field, not the potential, so R is false.

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a thin rod about an axis passing through its mid point and perpendicular to the rod, is 2400 g cm². The length of the 400 g rod is nearly:
questions.sol: \(I = \dfrac{ML^2}{12} \Rightarrow L^2 = \dfrac{12\times2400}{400} = 72\ \text{cm}^2 \Rightarrow L \approx 8.5\) cm.

questions.q: The terminal voltage of the battery, whose emf is 10 V and internal resistance 1 Ω, when connected through an external resistance of 4 Ω as shown in the figure is:
questions.sol: \(I = \dfrac{E}{R + r} = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2\) A. Terminal voltage \(V = E - Ir = 10 - 2 = 8\) V.

questions.q:
Match the List-I with List-II.
List-I (Spectral lines of hydrogen for transitions from)List-II (Wavelengths (nm))
(A) \(n_2 = 3\) to \(n_1 = 2\)(I) 410.2
(B) \(n_2 = 4\) to \(n_1 = 2\)(II) 434.1
(C) \(n_2 = 5\) to \(n_1 = 2\)(III) 656.3
(D) \(n_2 = 6\) to \(n_1 = 2\)(IV) 486.1
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Balmer lines: 3→2 is \(H_\alpha\) = 656.3 nm, 4→2 = 486.1 nm, 5→2 = 434.1 nm, 6→2 = 410.2 nm. So A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

questions.q:
If \(c\) is the velocity of light in free space, the correct statements about photon among the following are:
A. The energy of a photon is \(E = h\nu\).
B. The velocity of a photon is \(c\).
C. The momentum of a photon, \(p = \dfrac{h\nu}{c}\).
D. In a photon-electron collision, both total energy and total momentum are conserved.
E. Photon possesses positive charge.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: A, B, D and E only
A, B, C and D only
questions.sol: A, B, C and D are standard properties of photons (energy and momentum are both conserved in photon–electron collisions). E is wrong: a photon has no charge.

questions.q:
\({}^{290}_{82}X \xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ } Y \xrightarrow{\ e^+\ } Z \xrightarrow{\ \beta^-\ } P \xrightarrow{\ e^-\ } Q\)
In the nuclear emission stated above, the mass number and atomic number of the product Q respectively, are:
questions.sol: \({}^{290}_{82}X \xrightarrow{\alpha} {}^{286}_{80}Y \xrightarrow{e^+} {}^{286}_{79}Z \xrightarrow{\beta^-} {}^{286}_{80}P \xrightarrow{e^-} {}^{286}_{81}Q\). Mass number 286, atomic number 81.

questions.q: At any instant of time \(t\), the displacement of any particle is given by \(2t - 1\) (SI unit) under the influence of force of 5 N. The value of instantaneous power is (in SI unit):
questions.sol: \(x = 2t - 1 \Rightarrow v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2\) m/s. Power \(P = Fv = 5\times2 = 10\) W.

questions.q: The output (Y) of the given logic gate is similar to the output of an/a:
questions.sol: A NAND gate with both inputs joined gives \(\bar A\); a NOR gate with both inputs joined gives \(\bar B\). The final NOR gives \(Y = \overline{\bar A + \bar B} = AB\): an AND gate.

questions.q: The mass of a planet is \(\frac{1}{10}\)th that of the earth and its diameter is half that of the earth. The acceleration due to gravity on that planet is:

Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Atoms are electrically neutral as they contain equal number of positive and negative charges.
Statement II: Atoms of each element are stable and emit their characteristic spectrum.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

questions.q: A wheel of a bullock cart is rolling on a level road as shown in the figure below. If its linear speed is \(v\) in the direction shown, which one of the following options is correct (P and Q are any highest and lowest points on the wheel respectively)?
o: Both the points P and Q move with equal speed.
Point P moves slower than point Q.
Point P moves faster than point Q.
questions.sol: In rolling without slipping, the top point moves at \(2v\) and the contact point is momentarily at rest. So P (top) moves faster than Q (bottom).

questions.q: A particle moving with uniform speed in a circular path maintains:
questions.sol: In uniform circular motion the speed is constant but the direction of velocity keeps changing, and the centripetal acceleration also keeps changing direction. Both vary.

questions.q: A thin flat circular disc of radius 4.5 cm is placed gently over the surface of water. If surface tension of water is \(0.07\ \text{N m}^{-1}\), then the excess force required to take it away from the surface is:
questions.sol: Surface tension acts along the rim: \(F = S\times2\pi r = 0.07\times2\pi\times0.045 \approx 1.98\times10^{-2}\) N = 19.8 mN.

questions.q: In a uniform magnetic field of 0.049 T, a magnetic needle performs 20 complete oscillations in 5 seconds as shown. The moment of inertia of the needle is \(9.8 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{kg m}^2\). If the magnitude of magnetic moment of the needle is \(x \times 10^{-5}\ \text{A m}^2\), then the value of \(x\) is:
questions.sol: \(T = \dfrac{5}{20} = 0.25\) s and \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{mB}} \Rightarrow m = \dfrac{4\pi^2 I}{T^2 B} = \dfrac{4\pi^2\times9.8\times10^{-6}}{0.0625\times0.049} = 1280\pi^2\times10^{-5}\ \text{A m}^2\).

questions.q: Two bodies A and B of same mass undergo completely inelastic one dimensional collision. The body A moves with velocity \(v_1\) while body B is at rest before collision. The velocity of the system after collision is \(v_2\). The ratio \(v_1 : v_2\) is:
questions.sol: Momentum conservation: \(mv_1 = 2m\,v_2 \Rightarrow v_1 : v_2 = 2 : 1\).

questions.q: If \(x = 5\sin\left(\pi t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\) m represents the motion of a particle executing simple harmonic motion, the amplitude and time period of motion, respectively, are:
questions.sol: Compare with \(x = A\sin(\omega t + \phi)\): \(A = 5\) m and \(\omega = \pi\), so \(T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\) s.

questions.q: The quantities which have the same dimensions as those of solid angle are:
questions.sol: Solid angle is dimensionless. Strain (a ratio of lengths) and angle (arc ÷ radius) are also dimensionless.

questions.q: A thin spherical shell is charged by some source. The potential difference between the two points C and P (in V) shown in the figure is: (Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^{9}\) SI units)
questions.sol: Inside a charged conducting shell the field is zero, so the potential everywhere inside equals the potential on the shell. C and P are at the same potential: the difference is zero.

questions.q: A bob is whirled in a horizontal plane by means of a string with an initial speed of \(\omega\) rpm. The tension in the string is \(T\). If speed becomes \(2\omega\) while keeping the same radius, the tension in the string becomes:
questions.sol: Tension \(T = m\omega^2 r\). Doubling \(\omega\) at the same radius makes the tension \(4T\).

questions.q: A wire of length \(l\) and resistance 100 Ω is divided into 10 equal parts. The first 5 parts are connected in series while the next 5 parts are connected in parallel. The two combinations are again connected in series. The resistance of this final combination is:
questions.sol: Each part is 10 Ω. Five in series = 50 Ω; five in parallel = 2 Ω. Total = 52 Ω.

questions.q: The following graph represents the T-V curves of an ideal gas (where T is the temperature and V the volume) at three pressures \(P_1\), \(P_2\) and \(P_3\) compared with those of Charles's law represented as dotted lines.
questions.sol: For an ideal gas \(T = \dfrac{P}{nR}V\), so the slope of a T–V line is proportional to pressure. The steepest curve has the largest pressure: \(P_1 > P_2 > P_3\).

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor is charged by connecting it to a battery through a resistor. If \(I\) is the current in the circuit, then in the gap between the plates:
o: displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in a direction opposite to that of I.
displacement current of magnitude greater than I flows but can be in any direction.
displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in the same direction as I.
questions.sol: Between the plates the conduction current is continued by the displacement current \(\varepsilon_0\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}\), which equals \(I\) and is in the same direction.

questions.q: The property which is not of an electromagnetic wave travelling in free space is that:
o: they travel with a speed equal to \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}}\)
they originate from charges moving with uniform speed.
their energy density in electric field is equal to energy density in magnetic field.
questions.sol: Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerated charges. Charges moving with uniform velocity do not radiate, so (2) is not a property of EM waves.

questions.q: Choose the correct circuit which can achieve the bridge balance.

If the plates of a parallel plate capacitor connected to a battery are moved close to each other, then
A. the charge stored in it, increases.
B. the energy stored in it, decreases.
C. its capacitance increases.
D. the ratio of charge to its potential remains the same.
E. the product of charge and voltage increases.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: Moving plates closer increases \(C\). At constant \(V\): \(Q = CV\) increases (A), energy \(\tfrac12CV^2\) increases (so B is wrong), \(Q/V = C\) changes (so D is wrong), \(QV\) increases (E). Correct: A, C and E.

questions.q: A force defined by \(F = \alpha t^2 + \beta t\) acts on a particle at a given time \(t\). The factor which is dimensionless, if \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are constants, is:
questions.sol: \(\alpha t^2\) and \(\beta t\) both have the dimensions of force, so \(\dfrac{\alpha t^2}{\beta t} = \dfrac{\alpha t}{\beta}\) is dimensionless.

questions.q: A metallic bar of Young's modulus \(0.5 \times 10^{11}\ \text{N m}^{-2}\) and coefficient of linear thermal expansion \(10^{-5}\ {}^\circ\text{C}^{-1}\), length 1 m and area of cross-section \(10^{-3}\ \text{m}^2\) is heated from 0 °C to 100 °C without expansion or bending. The compressive force developed in it is:
questions.sol: Thermal stress \(= Y\alpha\Delta T\). \(F = YA\alpha\Delta T = 0.5\times10^{11}\times10^{-3}\times10^{-5}\times100 = 5\times10^4\) N = \(50\times10^3\) N.

questions.q: A small telescope has an objective of focal length 140 cm and an eye piece of focal length 5.0 cm. The magnifying power of telescope for viewing a distant object is:
questions.sol: For a distant object \(M = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e} = \dfrac{140}{5} = 28\).

questions.q: An iron bar of length \(L\) has magnetic moment \(M\). It is bent at the middle of its length such that the two arms make an angle \(60^\circ\) with each other. The magnetic moment of this new magnet is:
questions.sol: Pole strength is unchanged. The two arms of length \(\tfrac L2\) at \(60^\circ\) form an equilateral triangle, so the poles are now \(\tfrac L2\) apart. New moment \(= \dfrac M2\).

questions.q: A 10 μF capacitor is connected to a 210 V, 50 Hz source as shown in figure. The peak current in the circuit is nearly (\(\pi = 3.14\)):
questions.sol: \(X_C = \dfrac{1}{2\pi fC} = \dfrac{1}{2\times3.14\times50\times10\times10^{-6}} \approx 318.5\) Ω. \(I_{\text{rms}} = \dfrac{210}{318.5} \approx 0.66\) A; peak \(= \sqrt2\times0.66 \approx 0.93\) A.

questions.q: Two heaters A and B have power rating of 1 kW and 2 kW, respectively. Those two are first connected in series and then in parallel to a fixed power source. The ratio of power outputs for these two cases is:
questions.sol: \(R = \dfrac{V^2}{P}\): \(R_A = \dfrac{V^2}{1}\), \(R_B = \dfrac{V^2}{2}\) (in kW units). Series: \(P_s = \dfrac{V^2}{R_A + R_B} = \dfrac23\) kW. Parallel: \(P_p = 1 + 2 = 3\) kW. Ratio \(= \dfrac{2/3}{3} = 2 : 9\).

questions.q: The velocity (\(v\))–time (\(t\)) plot of the motion of a body is shown below. The acceleration (\(a\))–time (\(t\)) graph that best suits this motion is:
questions.sol: The v–t graph rises linearly (constant positive \(a\)), stays flat (\(a = 0\)), then falls linearly (constant negative \(a\)). The a–t graph is a positive block, zero, then a negative block: graph (1).

questions.q: If the mass of the bob in simple pendulum is increased to thrice its original mass and its length is made half its original length, then the new time period of oscillation is \(\dfrac{x}{2}\) times its original time period. Then the value of \(x\) is:
questions.sol: \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{L/g}\) does not depend on mass. Halving \(L\): \(T' = \dfrac{T}{\sqrt2} = \dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}T\), so \(x = \sqrt2\).

questions.q: The minimum energy required to launch a satellite of mass \(m\) from the surface of earth of mass \(M\) and radius \(R\) in a circular orbit at an altitude of \(2R\) from the surface of the earth is:
questions.sol: In an orbit of radius \(3R\): \(E = -\dfrac{GMm}{2(3R)}\). On the surface: \(E = -\dfrac{GMm}{R}\). Energy needed \(= \dfrac{GMm}{R} - \dfrac{GMm}{6R} = \dfrac{5GMm}{6R}\).

questions.q:
A sheet is placed on a horizontal surface in front of a strong magnetic pole. A force is needed to:
A. hold the sheet there if it is magnetic.
B. hold the sheet there if it is non-magnetic.
C. move the sheet away from the pole with uniform velocity if it is conducting.
D. move the sheet away from the pole with uniform velocity if it is both, non-conducting and non-polar.
Choose the correct statement(s) from the options given below:
questions.sol: A magnetic sheet is attracted by the pole, so a force is needed to hold it (A). A conducting sheet moving in the field has eddy currents that oppose its motion, so a force is needed to move it (C). B and D need no force. Answer: A and C.

questions.q: The errors in the measurement which arise due to unpredictable fluctuations in temperature and voltage supply are:
questions.sol: Errors from unpredictable fluctuations (temperature, supply voltage) vary randomly from reading to reading: these are random errors.

questions.q: A metal wire has mass \((0.4 \pm 0.002)\) g, radius \((0.3 \pm 0.001)\) mm and length \((5 \pm 0.02)\) cm. The maximum possible percentage error in the measurement of density will nearly be:
questions.sol: \(\rho = \dfrac{m}{\pi r^2 l} \Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta\rho}{\rho} = \dfrac{\Delta m}{m} + 2\dfrac{\Delta r}{r} + \dfrac{\Delta l}{l} = \dfrac{0.002}{0.4} + 2\cdot\dfrac{0.001}{0.3} + \dfrac{0.02}{5} = 0.005 + 0.0067 + 0.004 \approx 1.6\%\).

questions.q: A vehicle travels half the distance with speed \(v\) and the remaining distance with speed \(2v\). Its average speed is:
questions.sol: For equal distances \(d\): \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v + d/2v} = \dfrac{2}{3/2v} = \dfrac{4v}{3}\).

questions.q: A football player is moving southward and suddenly turns eastward with the same speed to avoid an opponent. The force that acts on the player while turning is:
questions.sol: Initial velocity \(-v\hat j\) (south), final \(v\hat i\) (east). \(\Delta\vec v = v\hat i + v\hat j\), which points north-east. The force is along \(\Delta\vec v\): north-east.

questions.q: A bullet is fired from a gun at the speed of 280 m/s in the direction \(30^\circ\) above the horizontal. The maximum height attained by the bullet is (\(g = 9.8\ \text{m s}^{-2}\), \(\sin 30^\circ = 0.5\))
The potential energy of a long spring when stretched by 2 cm is \(U\). If the spring is stretched by 8 cm, potential energy stored in it will be:
questions.sol: \(U = \tfrac12kx^2 \propto x^2\). Stretch increases 4 times, so energy increases 16 times: \(16U\).

questions.q: The angular acceleration of a body, moving along the circumference of a circle, is:
o: along the radius, away from centre
along the radius towards the centre
along the tangent to its position
questions.sol: Angular acceleration is a vector along the axis of rotation (parallel or antiparallel to \(\vec\omega\)).

questions.q: The ratio of radius of gyration of a solid sphere of mass \(M\) and radius \(R\) about its own axis to the radius of gyration of the thin hollow sphere of same mass and radius about its axis is:
questions.sol: Solid sphere \(k_s = \sqrt{\tfrac25}R\); thin hollow sphere \(k_h = \sqrt{\tfrac23}R\). \(\dfrac{k_s}{k_h} = \sqrt{\dfrac35} = \sqrt3 : \sqrt5\), which is not among the printed options.
questions.note: None of the options as printed is correct: \(k_{\text{solid}} : k_{\text{hollow}} = \sqrt{2/5} : \sqrt{2/3} = \sqrt3 : \sqrt5\).

questions.q: Two bodies of mass \(m\) and \(9m\) are placed at a distance \(R\). The gravitational potential on the line joining the bodies where the gravitational field equals zero, will be (\(G\) = gravitational constant):
questions.sol: Field zero at distance \(x\) from \(m\): \(\dfrac{m}{x^2} = \dfrac{9m}{(R-x)^2} \Rightarrow R - x = 3x \Rightarrow x = \dfrac R4\). Potential there \(= -\dfrac{Gm}{R/4} - \dfrac{9Gm}{3R/4} = -\dfrac{4Gm}{R} - \dfrac{12Gm}{R} = -\dfrac{16Gm}{R}\).

questions.q: Let a wire be suspended from the ceiling (rigid support) and stretched by a weight \(W\) attached at its free end. The longitudinal stress at any point of cross-sectional area \(A\) of the wire is:
questions.sol: The wire is massless (only the weight \(W\) pulls it), so the tension is \(W\) everywhere. Stress \(= \dfrac{W}{A}\).

questions.q: The amount of energy required to form a bubble of radius 2 cm from a soap solution is nearly: (surface tension of soap solution = \(0.03\ \text{N m}^{-1}\))
questions.sol: A soap bubble has two surfaces: \(E = 2\times4\pi r^2 S = 8\pi(0.02)^2(0.03) \approx 3.01\times10^{-4}\) J.

questions.q: The venturi-meter works on:
questions.sol: A venturimeter measures flow speed from the pressure drop at the narrow throat, using Bernoulli's principle.

questions.q: A Carnot engine has an efficiency of 50% when its source is at a temperature 327 °C. The temperature of the sink is:
questions.sol: \(\eta = 1 - \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} \Rightarrow 0.5 = 1 - \dfrac{T_2}{600\text{ K}} \Rightarrow T_2 = 300\) K = 27 °C.

questions.q: The temperature of a gas is −50 °C. To what temperature the gas should be heated so that the rms speed is increased by 3 times?
questions.sol: \(v_{\text{rms}} \propto \sqrt T\). \(T_1 = 223\) K. If the speed becomes 4 times (\(v + 3v\)), \(T_2 = 16\times223 = 3568\) K = 3295 °C.
questions.note: Here “increased by 3 times” means the rms speed becomes 4 times, so \(T\) becomes 16 times: \(16 \times 223\ \text{K} = 3568\ \text{K} = 3295\ ^\circ\text{C}\).

questions.q: The ratio of frequencies of fundamental harmonic produced by an open pipe to that of a closed pipe having the same length is
questions.sol: Open pipe: \(f_o = \dfrac{v}{2L}\); closed pipe: \(f_c = \dfrac{v}{4L}\). Ratio \(= 2 : 1\).

questions.q: An electric dipole is placed at an angle of \(30^\circ\) with an electric field of intensity \(2 \times 10^{5}\ \text{N C}^{-1}\). It experiences a torque equal to 4 N m. Calculate the magnitude of charge on the dipole, if the dipole length is 2 cm.
questions.sol: \(\tau = pE\sin\theta = (q\times0.02)(2\times10^5)(\tfrac12) = 2000q = 4 \Rightarrow q = 2\times10^{-3}\) C = 2 mC.

questions.q: If \(\oint_S \vec E \cdot d\vec S = 0\) over a surface, then:
o: the electric field inside the surface is necessarily uniform.
the number of flux lines entering the surface must be equal to the number of flux lines leaving it.
the magnitude of electric field on the surface is constant.
all the charges must necessarily be inside the surface.
questions.sol: Zero net flux means as many field lines leave the surface as enter it (no net charge inside). It says nothing about the field being uniform or constant.

questions.q: The equivalent capacitance of the system shown in the following circuit is:
questions.sol: The two right-hand 3 μF capacitors are in parallel: 6 μF. In series with the left 3 μF: \(C = \dfrac{3\times6}{3+6} = 2\) μF.

questions.q: The magnitude and direction of the current in the following circuit is
o: 1.5 A from B to A through E
0.2 A from B to A through E
0.5 A from A to B through E
\(\dfrac{5}{9}\) A from A to B through E
questions.sol: The 10 V and 5 V cells oppose each other: net emf 5 V. Total resistance \(= 2 + 1 + 7 = 10\) Ω, so \(I = 0.5\) A. The 10 V cell drives it, so the current flows from A to B through E.

questions.q: If the galvanometer G does not show any deflection in the circuit shown, the value of R is given by:
questions.sol: No current through G, so the voltage across R equals 2 V. The current from the 10 V cell flows through 400 Ω and R: \(i = \dfrac{10 - 2}{400} = 0.02\) A, so \(R = \dfrac{2}{0.02} = 100\) Ω.

questions.q: Resistance of a carbon resistor determined from colour codes is \((22000 \pm 5\%)\ \Omega\). The colour of third band must be:
questions.sol: \(22000\ \Omega = 22\times10^3\ \Omega\): first two bands red (2) and red (2), multiplier \(10^3\) is orange.

questions.q: The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is:
questions.sol: Magnetic monopoles do not exist (Gauss's law for magnetism): the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero.

questions.q: The magnetic energy stored in an inductor of inductance 4 μH carrying a current of 2 A is:
questions.sol: \(U = \tfrac12LI^2 = \tfrac12\times4\times10^{-6}\times2^2 = 8\times10^{-6}\) J = 8 μJ.

questions.q: In a series LCR circuit, the inductance \(L\) is 10 mH, capacitance \(C\) is 1 μF and resistance \(R\) is 100 Ω. The frequency at which resonance occurs is:
questions.sol: \(f_0 = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{10^{-2}\times10^{-6}}} = \dfrac{10^4}{2\pi} \approx 1.59\times10^3\) Hz = 1.59 kHz.

questions.q: A 12 V, 60 W lamp is connected to the secondary of a step down transformer, whose primary is connected to ac mains of 220 V. Assuming the transformer to be ideal, what is the current in the primary winding?
questions.sol: Ideal transformer: input power = output power = 60 W. \(I_p = \dfrac{60}{220} \approx 0.27\) A.

questions.q: An ac source is connected to a capacitor C. Due to decrease in its operating frequency:
questions.sol: \(X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}\) increases when frequency falls, so the current (equal to the displacement current between the plates) decreases.

questions.q: In a plane electromagnetic wave travelling in free space, the electric field component oscillates sinusoidally at a frequency of \(2.0 \times 10^{10}\) Hz and amplitude \(48\ \text{V m}^{-1}\). Then the amplitude of oscillating magnetic field is: (Speed of light in free space \(= 3 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}\))
Light travels a distance \(x\) in time \(t_1\) in air and \(10x\) in time \(t_2\) in another denser medium. What is the critical angle for this medium?
questions.sol: Speed in air \(\dfrac{x}{t_1}\); in the medium \(\dfrac{10x}{t_2}\). \(\mu = \dfrac{x/t_1}{10x/t_2} = \dfrac{t_2}{10t_1}\), and \(\sin C = \dfrac{1}{\mu} = \dfrac{10t_1}{t_2}\).

questions.q:
For Young's double slit experiment, two statements are given below:
Statement I: If screen is moved away from the plane of slits, angular separation of the fringes remains constant.
Statement II: If the monochromatic source is replaced by another monochromatic source of larger wavelength, the angular separation of fringes decreases.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.sol: Angular fringe separation \(\theta = \dfrac{\lambda}{d}\) does not depend on screen distance: I is true. Larger \(\lambda\) gives larger \(\theta\), so II is false.

questions.q: The minimum wavelength of X-rays produced by an electron accelerated through a potential difference of \(V\) volts is proportional to:
questions.sol: \(\lambda_{\min} = \dfrac{hc}{eV} \propto \dfrac1V\).
