questions.q: The work functions of Caesium (Cs), Potassium (K) and Sodium (Na) are 2.14 eV, 2.30 eV and 2.75 eV respectively. If incident electromagnetic radiation has an incident energy of 2.20 eV, which of these photosensitive surfaces may emit photoelectrons?
questions.sol: Emission needs photon energy greater than the work function. 2.20 eV exceeds only 2.14 eV (Cs).

questions.q: In hydrogen spectrum, the shortest wavelength in the Balmer series is \(\lambda\). The shortest wavelength in the Brackett series is:
questions.sol: Shortest wavelength = series limit. Balmer: \(\dfrac1\lambda = \dfrac{R}{4}\); Brackett (\(n = 4\)): \(\dfrac{1}{\lambda'} = \dfrac{R}{16}\). So \(\lambda' = 4\lambda\).

questions.q: The half life of a radioactive substance is 20 minutes. In how much time, the activity of substance drops to \(\left(\frac{1}{16}\right)^{\text{th}}\) of its initial value?
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{1}{16} = \left(\dfrac12\right)^4\): four half-lives, \(4\times20 = 80\) minutes.

questions.q: A full wave rectifier circuit consists of two p-n junction diodes, a centre-tapped transformer, capacitor and a load resistance. Which of these components remove the ac ripple from the rectified output?
questions.sol: The capacitor filter charges at the peaks and discharges slowly between them, smoothing out the ripple.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Photovoltaic devices can convert optical radiation into electricity.
Statement II: Zener diode is designed to operate under reverse bias in breakdown region.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
questions.sol: Photovoltaic devices (solar cells) convert light into electricity, and a Zener diode is designed to work in reverse breakdown. Both statements are correct.

questions.q: A horizontal bridge is built across a river. A student standing on the bridge throws a small ball vertically upwards with a velocity \(4\ \text{m s}^{-1}\). The ball strikes the water surface after 4 s. The height of bridge above water surface is (Take \(g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}\)):
questions.sol: Taking up as positive: \(s = ut - \tfrac12gt^2 = 4\times4 - 5\times16 = -64\) m. The bridge is 64 m above the water.

questions.q: Calculate the maximum acceleration of a moving car so that a body lying on the floor of the car remains stationary. The coefficient of static friction between the body and the floor is 0.15 (\(g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}\)).
questions.sol: Friction gives the body its acceleration: \(a_{\max} = \mu g = 0.15\times10 = 1.5\ \text{m s}^{-2}\).

questions.q: A bullet from a gun is fired on a rectangular wooden block with velocity \(u\). When bullet travels 24 cm through the block along its length horizontally, velocity of bullet becomes \(\dfrac{u}{3}\). Then it further penetrates into the block in the same direction before coming to rest exactly at the other end of the block. The total length of the block is:
questions.sol: Over the first 24 cm: \(u^2 - \dfrac{u^2}{9} = 2a(24) \Rightarrow \dfrac{8u^2}{9} = 48a\). For the rest: \(\dfrac{u^2}{9} = 2ax \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{48a/8}{2a} = 3\) cm. Total length = 27 cm.

questions.q: A satellite is orbiting just above the surface of the earth with period \(T\). If \(d\) is the density of the earth and \(G\) is the universal constant of gravitation, the quantity \(\dfrac{3\pi}{Gd}\) represents:
questions.sol: For an orbit just above the surface \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R^3}{GM}}\), with \(M = \tfrac43\pi R^3 d\). So \(T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2R^3}{G\cdot\frac43\pi R^3d} = \dfrac{3\pi}{Gd}\).

questions.q: The \(x\)–\(t\) graph of a particle performing simple harmonic motion is shown in the figure. The acceleration of the particle at \(t = 2\) s is:
questions.sol: From the graph, amplitude 1 m and period 8 s, so \(\omega = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\). At \(t = 2\) s, \(x = +1\) m: \(a = -\omega^2x = -\dfrac{\pi^2}{16}\ \text{m s}^{-2}\).

questions.q: An electric dipole is placed as shown in the figure. The electric potential (in \(10^2\) V) at point P due to the dipole is (\(\varepsilon_0\) = permittivity of free space and \(\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = K\)):
questions.sol: P is 5 cm from the centre: 2 cm from \(+q\) and 8 cm from \(-q\). \(V = Kq\left(\dfrac{1}{0.02} - \dfrac{1}{0.08}\right) = 37.5\,Kq = \dfrac38qK\times10^2\) V.

questions.q: The resistance of platinum wire at 0 °C is 2 Ω and 6.8 Ω at 80 °C. The temperature coefficient of resistance of the wire is:

10 resistors, each of resistance \(R\) are connected in series to a battery of emf \(E\) and negligible internal resistance. Then those are connected in parallel to the same battery, the current is increased \(n\) times. The value of \(n\) is:
questions.sol: Series: \(10R\), so \(I_s = \dfrac{E}{10R}\). Parallel: \(\dfrac{R}{10}\), so \(I_p = \dfrac{10E}{R}\). \(n = \dfrac{I_p}{I_s} = 100\).

questions.q: A very long conducting wire is bent in a semi-circular shape from A to B as shown in figure. The magnetic field at point P for steady current configuration is given by:
o: \(\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4R}\) pointed away from the page
\(\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4R}\left[1 - \dfrac{2}{\pi}\right]\) pointed away from the page
questions.sol: Arc: \(\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4R}\), out of the page (current circulates anticlockwise about P). Each straight wire ends level with P and gives \(\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi R}\) into the page; together \(\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi R}\). Net \(= \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4R}\left(1 - \dfrac2\pi\right)\), away from (out of) the page.

questions.q: A wire carrying a current \(I\) along the positive \(x\)-axis has length \(L\). It is kept in a magnetic field \(\vec B = (2\hat i + 3\hat j - 4\hat k)\) T. The magnitude of the magnetic force acting on the wire is:
questions.sol: \(\vec F = IL\hat i\times(2\hat i + 3\hat j - 4\hat k) = IL(3\hat k + 4\hat j)\). \(|\vec F| = IL\sqrt{9 + 16} = 5IL\).

questions.q: The net impedance of circuit (as shown in figure) will be:
questions.sol: \(X_L = 2\pi\times50\times\dfrac{50}{\pi}\times10^{-3} = 5\) Ω; \(X_C = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\times50\times\frac{10^3}{\pi}\times10^{-6}} = 10\) Ω. \(Z = \sqrt{10^2 + (10 - 5)^2} = 5\sqrt5\) Ω.

questions.q: In the figure shown here, what is the equivalent focal length of the combination of lenses (Assume that all layers are thin)?
questions.sol: Three thin lenses in contact. Glass biconvex: \(\dfrac1f = (1.5 - 1)\dfrac{2}{20} = 0.05\). Each liquid layer is plano-concave: \((1.6 - 1)\left(-\dfrac{1}{20}\right) = -0.03\), two of them \(-0.06\). Total \(\dfrac1F = -0.01\ \text{cm}^{-1} \Rightarrow F = -100\) cm.

questions.q: Two thin lenses are of same focal lengths (\(f\)), but one is convex and the other one is concave. When they are placed in contact with each other, the equivalent focal length of the combination will be:
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1F = \dfrac1f - \dfrac1f = 0\): zero power, so the focal length is infinite.

questions.q: The radius of inner most orbit of hydrogen atom is \(5.3 \times 10^{-11}\) m. What is the radius of third allowed orbit of hydrogen atom?
For the following logic circuit, the truth table is:
questions.sol: The NOT gates give \(\bar A\) and \(\bar B\); the NAND gives \(Y = \overline{\bar A\bar B} = A + B\). That is OR: Y = 0 only when A = B = 0, which is table (3).

questions.q: Plane angle and solid angle have:
questions.sol: Plane angle (radian) and solid angle (steradian) have units, but as ratios (arc/radius, area/radius²) they are dimensionless.

questions.q: The dimension \([\text{MLT}^{-2}\text{A}^{-2}]\) belongs to the:
questions.sol: \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} \Rightarrow \mu_0 = \dfrac{[\text{MT}^{-2}\text{A}^{-1}][\text{L}]}{[\text{A}]} = [\text{MLT}^{-2}\text{A}^{-2}]\): magnetic permeability.

questions.q: The ratio of the distance travelled by a freely falling body in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th second:
questions.sol: From rest, distance in the \(n\)-th second \(\propto (2n - 1)\): 1 : 3 : 5 : 7.

questions.q: The displacement-time graphs of two moving particles make angles of \(30^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\) with the x-axis as shown in the figure. The ratio of their respective velocity is:
questions.sol: Slope of a displacement–time graph = velocity: \(\dfrac{v_1}{v_2} = \dfrac{\tan30^\circ}{\tan45^\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\).

questions.q: A shell of mass \(m\) is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having mass in the ratio 2 : 2 : 1. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed \(v\), the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is:
questions.sol: Masses \(\dfrac{2m}{5}, \dfrac{2m}{5}, \dfrac m5\). The two equal fragments have perpendicular momenta \(\dfrac{2m}{5}v\) each, resultant \(\dfrac{2\sqrt2\,m v}{5}\). The light piece balances it: \(\dfrac m5 v' = \dfrac{2\sqrt2\,mv}{5} \Rightarrow v' = 2\sqrt2\,v\).

questions.q: An electric lift with a maximum load of 2000 kg (lift + passengers) is moving up with a constant speed of \(1.5\ \text{m s}^{-1}\). The frictional force opposing the motion is 3000 N. The minimum power delivered by the motor to the lift in watts is: (\(g = 10\ \text{m s}^{-2}\))
questions.sol: At constant speed the motor force = weight + friction = 20000 + 3000 = 23000 N. \(P = Fv = 23000\times1.5 = 34500\) W.

questions.q: The energy that will be ideally radiated by a 100 kW transmitter in 1 hour is:
The angular speed of a fly wheel moving with uniform angular acceleration changes from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 seconds. The angular acceleration in \(\text{rad/s}^2\) is:
questions.sol: \(\Delta\omega = \dfrac{(3120 - 1200)\times2\pi}{60} = 64\pi\) rad/s. \(\alpha = \dfrac{64\pi}{16} = 4\pi\ \text{rad/s}^2\).

questions.q: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a thin uniform disc about an axis passing through its centre and normal to its plane to the radius of gyration of the disc about its diameter is:
questions.sol: About the normal axis \(I = \tfrac12MR^2\), so \(k_1 = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt2}\). About a diameter \(I = \tfrac14MR^2\), so \(k_2 = \dfrac R2\). \(\dfrac{k_1}{k_2} = \sqrt2 : 1\).

questions.q: Two objects of mass 10 kg and 20 kg respectively are connected to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 10 m with negligible mass. The distance of the centre of mass of the system from the 10 kg mass is:
questions.sol: \(x_{\text{cm}} = \dfrac{20\times10}{10 + 20} = \dfrac{20}{3}\) m from the 10 kg mass.

questions.q: A body of mass 60 g experiences a gravitational force of 3.0 N, when placed at a particular point. The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at that point is:
questions.sol: Field intensity \(= \dfrac Fm = \dfrac{3.0}{0.06} = 50\) N/kg.

questions.q: A spherical ball is dropped in a long column of a highly viscous liquid. The curve in the graph shown which represents the speed of the ball (\(v\)) as a function of time (\(t\)) is:
questions.sol: The ball speeds up from rest, but viscous drag grows with speed until it reaches a constant terminal velocity. The curve rises and then levels off: curve B.

questions.q: If a soap bubble expands, the pressure inside the bubble:
o: is equal to the atmospheric pressure
questions.sol: Excess pressure inside a bubble is \(\dfrac{4S}{r}\). As the bubble expands \(r\) increases, so the pressure inside decreases.

questions.q: An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state as shown in the figure below. Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is:
questions.sol: Curve 1 is vertical (isochoric) and curve 4 horizontal (isobaric). Of the two falling curves, the adiabatic one is steeper (\(\gamma > 1\)): curve 2.

questions.q: If the initial tension on a stretched string is doubled, then the ratio of the initial and final speed of a transverse wave along the string is:
questions.sol: \(v = \sqrt{T/\mu} \propto \sqrt T\). Doubling \(T\): \(v_i : v_f = 1 : \sqrt2\).

questions.q: Two hollow conducting spheres of radii \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) (\(R_1 \gg R_2\)) have equal charges. The potential would be:
o: dependent on the material property of the sphere
questions.sol: Potential of a sphere \(V = \dfrac{kq}{R}\). Equal charges, so the smaller sphere (\(R_2\)) has the higher potential.

questions.q: The angle between the electric lines of force and the equipotential surface is:
questions.sol: Electric field lines are always perpendicular to equipotential surfaces: \(90^\circ\).

questions.q: As the temperature increases, the electrical resistance:
o: decreases for conductors but increases for semiconductors
increases for both conductors and semiconductors
decreases for both conductors and semiconductors
increases for conductors but decreases for semiconductors
questions.sol: In conductors more lattice vibrations raise resistance. In semiconductors more charge carriers are freed, so resistance falls.

questions.q: A copper wire of length 10 m and radius \((10^{-2}/\sqrt\pi)\) m has electrical resistance of 10 Ω. The current density in the wire for an electric field strength of 10 V/m is:
Two resistors of resistance 100 Ω and 200 Ω are connected in parallel in an electrical circuit. The ratio of the thermal energy developed in 100 Ω to that in 200 Ω in a given time is:
questions.sol: In parallel the voltage is the same: \(H = \dfrac{V^2t}{R} \propto \dfrac1R\). \(H_{100} : H_{200} = 2 : 1\).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Biot-Savart's law gives us the expression for the magnetic field strength of an infinitesimal current element (\(I\,d\vec l\)) of the current carrying conductor only.
Statement II: Biot-Savart's law is analogous to Coulomb's inverse square law of charge \(q\), with the former being related to the field produced by a scalar source, \(I\,d\vec l\), while the latter being produced by a vector source, \(q\).
In light of above statements choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
questions.sol: Statement I is correct. Statement II has it backwards: the current element \(I\,d\vec l\) is a vector source, while charge \(q\) is a scalar source.

questions.q: A long solenoid of radius 1 mm has 100 turns per mm. If 1 A current flows in the solenoid, the magnetic field strength at the centre of the solenoid is:
questions.sol: \(n = 100\) per mm \(= 10^5\) per m. \(B = \mu_0nI = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\times10^5\times1 \approx 12.56\times10^{-2}\) T.

questions.q: A square loop of side 1 m and resistance 1 Ω is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is:
questions.sol: Field normal to the loop: \(\Phi = BA = 0.5\times1^2 = 0.5\) Wb.

questions.q: The peak voltage of the ac source is equal to
o: \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\) times the rms value of the source
the value of voltage supplied to the circuit
the rms value of the ac source
\(\sqrt2\) times the rms value of the ac source
questions.sol: \(V_0 = \sqrt2\,V_{\text{rms}}\).

questions.q: When light propagates through a material medium of relative permittivity \(\varepsilon_r\) and relative permeability \(\mu_r\), the velocity of light, \(v\) is given by: (\(c\) – velocity of light in vacuum)
questions.sol: \(v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu\varepsilon}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}\sqrt{\mu_r\varepsilon_r}} = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_r\mu_r}}\).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Electromagnetic waves)List-II (Wavelength)
(a) AM radio waves(i) \(10^{-10}\) m
(b) Microwaves(ii) \(10^{2}\) m
(c) Infrared radiations(iii) \(10^{-2}\) m
(d) X-rays(iv) \(10^{-4}\) m
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: AM radio \(\sim10^2\) m (ii), microwaves \(\sim10^{-2}\) m (iii), infrared \(\sim10^{-4}\) m (iv), X-rays \(\sim10^{-10}\) m (i).

questions.q: A biconvex lens has radii of curvature, 20 cm each. If the refractive index of the material of the lens is 1.5, the power of the lens is:
questions.sol: \(\dfrac1f = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right) = 0.5\times\dfrac{2}{0.2} = 5\ \text{m}^{-1}\): power +5 D.

questions.q: A light ray falls on a glass surface of refractive index \(\sqrt3\), at an angle \(60^\circ\). The angle between the refracted and reflected rays would be:
questions.sol: \(\tan60^\circ = \sqrt3 = \mu\), so the ray is at Brewster's angle. At Brewster's angle the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular: \(90^\circ\).

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment, a student observes 8 fringes in a certain segment of screen when a monochromatic light of 600 nm wavelength is used. If the wavelength of light is changed to 400 nm, then the number of fringes he would observe in the same region of the screen is
questions.sol: Fringe width \(\beta \propto \lambda\), so the number of fringes in a fixed length is \(\propto \dfrac1\lambda\): \(n = 8\times\dfrac{600}{400} = 12\).

questions.q: The graph which shows the variation of the de Broglie wavelength (\(\lambda\)) of a particle and its associated momentum (\(p\)) is:
questions.sol: \(\lambda = \dfrac hp\): \(\lambda\) is inversely proportional to \(p\), a rectangular hyperbola (graph a).

questions.q: When two monochromatic lights of frequency \(\nu\) and \(\nu/2\) are incident on a photoelectric metal, their stopping potential becomes \(V_s/2\) and \(V_s\) respectively. The threshold frequency for this metal is:
questions.sol:
Einstein's equation \(eV_s = h
u - h
u_0\) gives a larger stopping potential for a higher frequency. Here the higher frequency \(
u\) is given the smaller potential \(V_s/2\), so the data are inconsistent and no option can be derived.
questions.note: As printed, the higher frequency gives the smaller stopping potential, which is impossible, so none of the options can be derived; the source book also gives no answer.

questions.q: Let \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) be the energy of an electron in the first and second excited states of hydrogen atom, respectively. According to the Bohr's model of an atom, the ratio \(T_1 : T_2\) is:
questions.sol: First excited state \(n = 2\), second excited state \(n = 3\). \(E \propto \dfrac{1}{n^2}\): \(T_1 : T_2 = \dfrac14 : \dfrac19 = 9 : 4\).

questions.q: In the given nuclear reaction, the element X is: \({}^{22}_{11}\text{Na} \rightarrow X + e^{+} + \nu\)
questions.sol: In \(\beta^+\) decay a proton becomes a neutron: Z falls by 1, A is unchanged. \({}^{22}_{11}\text{Na} \to {}^{22}_{10}\text{Ne} + e^+ + \nu\).
questions.note: Options (3) and (4) are printed the same in the source paper; the answer is neon-22.

questions.q: In half wave rectification, if the input frequency is 60 Hz, then the output frequency would be:
questions.sol: A half-wave rectifier passes one half of every cycle, so the output repeats at the input frequency: 60 Hz.

questions.q: In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), the potential drop across the two p-n junctions are equal in:
questions.sol: In (a) and (c) both junctions face the same way, so both are forward biased (or both reverse) and have equal drops. In (b) one is forward and one reverse biased, so the drops differ.

questions.q: The area of a rectangular field (in m²) of length 55.3 m and breadth 25 m after rounding off the value for correct significant digits is:
questions.sol: \(55.3\times25 = 1382.5\ \text{m}^2\). The answer can have only 2 significant figures (as in 25): \(1.4\times10^3 = 14\times10^2\ \text{m}^2\).

questions.q: A ball is projected with a velocity, \(10\ \text{m s}^{-1}\), at an angle of \(60^\circ\) with the vertical direction. Its speed at the highest point of its trajectory will be:
questions.sol: \(60^\circ\) with the vertical is \(30^\circ\) with the horizontal. At the top only the horizontal part remains: \(10\cos30^\circ = 5\sqrt3\ \text{m s}^{-1}\).

questions.q:
Match List-I and List-II.
List-IList-II
(a) Gravitational constant (G)(i) \([\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]\)
(b) Gravitational potential energy(ii) \([\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]\)
(c) Gravitational potential(iii) \([\text{LT}^{-2}]\)
(d) Gravitational intensity(iv) \([\text{ML}^2\text{T}^{-2}]\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol: \(G\): \([\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^3\text{T}^{-2}]\) (ii); gravitational PE: \([\text{ML}^2\text{T}^{-2}]\) (iv); potential \(= \dfrac{\text{energy}}{\text{mass}}\): \([\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]\) (i); intensity \(= \dfrac{\text{force}}{\text{mass}}\): \([\text{LT}^{-2}]\) (iii).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The stretching of a spring is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the spring.
Reason (R): A coil spring of copper has more tensile strength than a steel spring of same dimensions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.sol: When a coil spring stretches, its wire twists, so the shear modulus decides the stretching: A is true. Steel springs are used because steel is stronger than copper: R is false.

questions.q: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP, if the intermolecular forces vanish away is:
questions.sol: 4.5 kg of water is 250 mol. As an ideal gas at STP: \(250\times22.4\) L = 5600 L = 5.6 m³.

questions.q: Two pendulums of length 121 cm and 100 cm start vibrating in phase. At some instant, the two are at their mean position in the same phase. The minimum number of vibrations of the shorter pendulum after which the two are again in phase at the mean position is:
questions.sol: \(T \propto \sqrt L\), so \(T_{121} : T_{100} = 11 : 10\). They are in phase again when \(n\) swings of the shorter equal \(n - 1\) swings of the longer: \(10n = 11(n - 1) \Rightarrow n = 11\).

questions.q: Two point charges \(-q\) and \(+q\) are placed at a distance of \(L\), as shown in the figure. The magnitude of electric field intensity at a distance \(R\) (\(R \gg L\)) varies as
questions.sol: Far from a dipole (\(R \gg L\)) the field falls as \(\dfrac{2kp}{R^3}\), i.e. \(\propto \dfrac{1}{R^3}\).

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance \(C\) = 900 pF is charged fully by 100 V battery B as shown in figure (a). Then it is disconnected from the battery and connected to another uncharged capacitor of capacitance \(C\) = 900 pF as shown in figure (b). The electrostatic energy stored by the system (b) is
questions.sol: \(Q = CV = 900\ \text{pF}\times100\ \text{V}\). Shared equally between two equal capacitors: each at 50 V. Energy \(= 2\times\tfrac12\times900\times10^{-12}\times50^2 = 2.25\times10^{-6}\) J.

questions.q: A wheatstone bridge is used to determine the value of unknown resistance X by adjusting the variable resistance Y as shown in the figure. For the most precise measurement of X, the resistances P and Q:
o: do not play any significant role
should be approximately equal and are small
should be very large and unequal
questions.sol: A Wheatstone bridge is most sensitive when all four arms are of comparable value. For the most precise measurement the ratio arms P and Q should be about equal and small.

questions.q: From Ampere's circuital law for a long straight wire of circular cross section carrying a steady current, the variation of magnetic field in the inside and outside region of the wire is:
o: a linearly decreasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then a linearly increasing one for the outside region.
uniform and remains constant for both the regions.
a linearly increasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then decreasing outside region.
a linearly increasing function of distance \(r\) upto the boundary of the wire and then \(1/r\) dependence for the outside region.
questions.sol: Ampere's law: inside the wire \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0Ir}{2\pi a^2} \propto r\); outside \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r} \propto \dfrac1r\).

questions.q: A big circular coil of 1000 turns and average radius 10 m is rotating about its horizontal diameter at 2 rad s⁻¹. If the vertical component of earth's magnetic field at that place is \(2 \times 10^{-5}\) T and electrical resistance of the coil is 12.56 Ω, then the maximum induced current in the coil will be:
questions.sol: \(\varepsilon_{\max} = NBA\omega = 1000\times2\times10^{-5}\times\pi(10)^2\times2 \approx 12.57\) V. \(I = \dfrac{12.57}{12.56} \approx 1\) A.

questions.q: A series LCR circuit with inductance 10 H, capacitance 10 μF, resistance 50 Ω is connected to an ac source of voltage, \(V = 200\sin(100t)\) volt. If the resonant frequency of the LCR circuit is \(\nu_0\) and the frequency of the ac source is \(\nu\), then:
questions.sol: Resonance: \(\omega_0 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10\times10\times10^{-6}}} = 100\) rad/s, so \(\nu_0 = \dfrac{50}{\pi}\) Hz. The source has \(\omega = 100\) rad/s, so \(\nu = \dfrac{50}{\pi}\) Hz too.

questions.q: Two transparent media A and B are separated by a plane boundary. The speed of light in those media are \(1.5 \times 10^{8}\) m/s and \(2.0 \times 10^{8}\) m/s, respectively. The critical angle for a ray of light for these two media is:
questions.sol: Light is slower in A, so A is denser. \(\sin C = \dfrac{v_A}{v_B} = \dfrac{1.5}{2.0} = 0.75 \Rightarrow C = \sin^{-1}(0.750)\).

questions.q: A nucleus of mass number 189 splits into two nuclei having mass number 125 and 64. The ratio of radius of two daughter nuclei respectively is:
questions.sol: \(R \propto A^{1/3}\): \(\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \left(\dfrac{125}{64}\right)^{1/3} = \dfrac54\).

questions.q: The truth table for the given logic circuit is:
questions.sol: Upper NAND: \(\overline{AB}\). Lower NAND: \(\overline{\bar A B}\). AND of the two: \(C = \overline{AB}\cdot\overline{\bar AB} = \overline{AB + \bar AB} = \overline{B}\). C is 1 when B = 0: table (4).

questions.q: A wire of length \(L\), area of cross section \(A\) is hanging from a fixed support. The length of the wire changes to \(L_1\) when mass \(M\) is suspended from its free end. The expression for Young's modulus is:
questions.sol: \(Y = \dfrac{\text{stress}}{\text{strain}} = \dfrac{Mg/A}{(L_1 - L)/L} = \dfrac{MgL}{A(L_1 - L)}\).

questions.q: A cylinder contains hydrogen gas at pressure of 249 kPa and temperature 27 °C. Its density is: (\(R = 8.3\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\))
questions.sol: \(\rho = \dfrac{PM}{RT} = \dfrac{249\times10^3\times2\times10^{-3}}{8.3\times300} = \dfrac{498}{2490} = 0.2\ \text{kg/m}^3\).

questions.q: Light with an average flux of \(20\ \text{W/cm}^2\) falls on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence having surface area \(20\ \text{cm}^2\). The energy received by the surface during time span of 1 minute is:
questions.sol: Power received \(= 20\ \text{W/cm}^2\times20\ \text{cm}^2 = 400\) W. Energy in 60 s \(= 400\times60 = 24\times10^3\) J.

questions.q: Two bodies of mass 4 kg and 6 kg are tied to the ends of a massless string. The string passes over a pulley which is frictionless (see figure). The acceleration of the system in terms of acceleration due to gravity (\(g\)) is:
The mean free path for a gas, with molecular diameter \(d\) and number density \(n\) can be expressed as:
questions.sol: Mean free path \(\lambda = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2\,n\pi d^2}\).

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically downward with a velocity of 20 m/s from the top of a tower. It hits the ground after some time with a velocity of 80 m/s. The height of the tower is: (\(g = 10\ \text{m/s}^2\))
questions.sol: \(v^2 = u^2 + 2gh \Rightarrow 6400 = 400 + 20h \Rightarrow h = 300\) m.

questions.q: The color code of a resistance is given below. The values of resistance and tolerance, respectively, are:
questions.sol: Yellow (4), Violet (7), Brown (×10): \(47\times10 = 470\) Ω. Gold band: ±5%.

questions.q: When a uranium isotope \({}^{235}_{92}\text{U}\) is bombarded with a neutron, it generates \({}^{89}_{36}\text{Kr}\), three neutrons and:

A spherical conductor of radius 10 cm has a charge of \(3.2 \times 10^{-7}\) C distributed uniformly. What is the magnitude of electric field at a point 15 cm from the centre of the sphere? \(\left(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^{9}\ \text{N m}^2/\text{C}^2\right)\)
questions.sol: Outside the sphere, treat the charge as a point charge: \(E = \dfrac{kq}{r^2} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times3.2\times10^{-7}}{(0.15)^2} = 1.28\times10^5\) N/C.

questions.q: A ray is incident at an angle of incidence \(i\) on one surface of a small angle prism (with angle of prism \(A\)) and emerges normally from the opposite surface. If the refractive index of the material of the prism is \(\mu\), then the angle of incidence is nearly equal to:
questions.sol: Emerging normally means \(r_2 = 0\), so \(r_1 = A\). For small angles \(i = \mu r_1 = \mu A\).

questions.q: Two cylinders A and B of equal capacity are connected to each other via a stop cock. A contains an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure. B is completely evacuated. The entire system is thermally insulated. The stop cock is suddenly opened. The process is:
questions.sol: The system is thermally insulated, so no heat enters or leaves (\(Q = 0\)): the free expansion is adiabatic.

questions.q: An iron rod of susceptibility 599 is subjected to a magnetising field of \(1200\ \text{A m}^{-1}\). The permeability of the material of the rod is: (\(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\ \text{T m A}^{-1}\))
The energy equivalent of 0.5 g of a substance is:
A 40 μF capacitor is connected to a 200 V, 50 Hz ac supply. The rms value of the current in the circuit is, nearly:
questions.sol: \(X_C = \dfrac{1}{2\pi fC} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\times50\times40\times10^{-6}} \approx 79.6\) Ω. \(I_{\text{rms}} = \dfrac{200}{79.6} \approx 2.5\) A.

questions.q: The ratio of contributions made by the electric field and magnetic field components to the intensity of an electromagnetic wave is: (\(c\) = speed of electromagnetic waves)
questions.sol: In an EM wave the electric and magnetic energy densities are equal (\(\tfrac12\varepsilon_0E^2 = \dfrac{B^2}{2\mu_0}\)), so they contribute equally: 1 : 1.

questions.q: Two particles of mass 5 kg and 10 kg respectively are attached to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 1 m with negligible mass. The centre of mass of the system from the 5 kg particle is nearly at a distance of:
questions.sol: \(x_{\text{cm}} = \dfrac{10\times1}{5 + 10} = \dfrac23\) m ≈ 67 cm from the 5 kg particle.

questions.q: A resistance wire connected in the left gap of a metre bridge balances a 10 Ω resistance in the right gap at a point which divides the bridge wire in the ratio 3 : 2. If the length of the resistance wire is 1.5 m, then the length of 1 Ω of the resistance wire is:
questions.sol: Balance: \(\dfrac{X}{10} = \dfrac32 \Rightarrow X = 15\) Ω for 1.5 m of wire, so 1 Ω is \(\dfrac{1.5}{15} = 0.1\) m = \(1.0\times10^{-1}\) m.

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, if the separation between coherent sources is halved and the distance of the screen from the coherent sources is doubled, then the fringe width becomes:
questions.sol: \(\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}\). Doubling \(D\) and halving \(d\) makes \(\beta\) four times as large.

questions.q: A charged particle having drift velocity of \(7.5 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{m s}^{-1}\) in an electric field of \(3 \times 10^{-10}\ \text{V m}^{-1}\), has a mobility in \(\text{m}^2\text{V}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\) of:
questions.sol: Mobility \(\mu = \dfrac{v_d}{E} = \dfrac{7.5\times10^{-4}}{3\times10^{-10}} = 2.5\times10^6\ \text{m}^2\text{V}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\).

questions.q: Dimensions of stress are:
questions.sol: Stress = force/area: \(\dfrac{[\text{MLT}^{-2}]}{[\text{L}^2]} = [\text{ML}^{-1}\text{T}^{-2}]\).

questions.q: For which one of the following, Bohr model is not valid?
questions.sol: Bohr's model works only for one-electron systems (H, He⁺, deuterium). Ne⁺ has many electrons.

questions.q: A series LCR circuit is connected to an ac voltage source. When \(L\) is removed from the circuit, the phase difference between current and voltage is \(\frac{\pi}{3}\). If instead \(C\) is removed from the circuit, the phase difference is again \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) between current and voltage. The power factor of the circuit is:
questions.sol: Removing L or removing C gives the same phase angle, so \(X_C = X_L\). The full circuit is at resonance: power factor = 1.

questions.q: A capillary tube of radius \(r\) is immersed in water and water rises in it to a height \(h\). The mass of the water in the capillary is 5 g. Another capillary tube of radius \(2r\) is immersed in water. The mass of water that will rise in this tube is:
questions.sol: Height \(h \propto \dfrac1r\), so mass \(\propto r^2h \propto r\). Doubling the radius doubles the mass: 10 g.

questions.q: Assume that light of wavelength 600 nm is coming from a star. The limit of resolution of telescope whose objective has a diameter of 2 m is:
questions.sol: \(\theta = \dfrac{1.22\lambda}{D} = \dfrac{1.22\times600\times10^{-9}}{2} = 3.66\times10^{-7}\) rad.

questions.q: The solids which have the negative temperature coefficient of resistance are:
questions.sol: Resistance falls with temperature in semiconductors and insulators (more carriers are freed). Metals have a positive coefficient.

questions.q: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with air as medium is 6 μF. With the introduction of a dielectric medium, the capacitance becomes 30 μF. The permittivity of the medium is: (\(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\ \text{C}^2\text{N}^{-1}\text{m}^{-2}\))
questions.sol: \(K = \dfrac{30}{6} = 5\). \(\varepsilon = K\varepsilon_0 = 5\times8.85\times10^{-12} \approx 0.44\times10^{-10}\ \text{C}^2\text{N}^{-1}\text{m}^{-2}\).

questions.q: The energy required to break one bond in DNA is \(10^{-20}\) J. This value in eV is nearly:
The increase in the width of the depletion region in a p-n junction diode is due to:
o: both forward bias and reverse bias
questions.sol: Reverse bias pulls carriers away from the junction, widening the depletion region. Forward bias narrows it.

questions.q: The quantities of heat required to raise the temperatures of two solid copper spheres of radii \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) (\(r_1 = 1.5\,r_2\)) through 1 K are in the ratio:
questions.sol: \(Q = mc\Delta T\) with \(m \propto r^3\): \(\dfrac{Q_1}{Q_2} = (1.5)^3 = \dfrac{27}{8}\).

questions.q: For the logic circuit shown, the truth table is:
questions.sol: The NOT gates give \(\bar A, \bar B\); the NOR gives \(Y = \overline{\bar A + \bar B} = AB\): an AND gate, table (4).

questions.q: For transistor action, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Base, emitter and collector regions should have same size.
Both emitter junction as well as the collector junction are forward biased.
The base region must be very thin and lightly doped.
Base, emitter and collector regions should have same doping concentrations.
questions.sol: For transistor action the base must be very thin and lightly doped, so most carriers pass from emitter to collector.

questions.q: In a guitar, two strings A and B made of same material are slightly out of tune and produce beats of frequency 6 Hz. When tension in B is slightly decreased, the beat frequency increases to 7 Hz. If the frequency of A is 530 Hz, the original frequency of B will be:
questions.sol: \(f_B = 530 \pm 6\): 524 or 536 Hz. Lowering the tension lowers \(f_B\); the beats increase to 7 only if \(f_B\) was below A: 524 → 523 Hz. Original \(f_B = 524\) Hz.

questions.q: A short electric dipole has a dipole moment of \(16 \times 10^{-9}\) C m. The electric potential due to the dipole at a point at a distance of 0.6 m from the centre of the dipole, situated on a line making an angle of \(60^\circ\) with the dipole axis is: \(\left(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^{9}\ \text{N m}^2/\text{C}^2\right)\)
questions.sol: \(V = \dfrac{kp\cos\theta}{r^2} = \dfrac{9\times10^9\times16\times10^{-9}\times0.5}{0.36} = 200\) V.

questions.q: A body weighs 72 N on the surface of the earth. What is the gravitational force on it, at a height equal to half the radius of the earth?
Which of the following graph represents the variation of resistivity (\(\rho\)) with temperature (\(T\)) for copper?
questions.sol: For a metal like copper, resistivity rises with temperature and curves upward at higher temperatures: graph (2).

questions.q: In a certain region of space with volume \(0.2\ \text{m}^3\), the electric potential is found to be 5 V throughout. The magnitude of electric field in this region is:
questions.sol: \(E = -\dfrac{dV}{dr}\). The potential is the same everywhere, so the field is zero.

questions.q: The average thermal energy for a mono-atomic gas is: (\(k_B\) is Boltzmann constant and \(T\), absolute temperature)
questions.sol: A monoatomic molecule has 3 translational degrees of freedom, each with \(\tfrac12k_BT\): average energy \(\tfrac32k_BT\).

questions.q: Find the torque about the origin when a force of \(3\hat j\) N acts on a particle whose position vector is \(2\hat k\) m.
questions.sol: \(\vec\tau = \vec r\times\vec F = 2\hat k\times3\hat j = 6(\hat k\times\hat j) = -6\hat i\) N m.

questions.q: Light of frequency 1.5 times the threshold frequency is incident on a photosensitive material. What will be the photoelectric current if the frequency is halved and intensity is doubled?
questions.sol: Halving \(1.5\nu_0\) gives \(0.75\nu_0\), below the threshold. No photoelectrons are emitted whatever the intensity: zero current.

questions.q: A long solenoid of 50 cm length having 100 turns carries a current of 2.5 A. The magnetic field at the centre of the solenoid is: (\(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\ \text{T m A}^{-1}\))
The Brewster's angle \(i_b\) for an interface should be:
questions.sol: \(\tan i_b = \mu > 1\) for light going into a denser medium, so \(45^\circ < i_b < 90^\circ\).

questions.q: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of \(V\) volt. If the de Broglie wavelength of the electron is \(1.227 \times 10^{-2}\) nm, the potential difference is:
questions.sol: For an electron \(\lambda = \dfrac{1.227}{\sqrt V}\) nm. \(\dfrac{1.227}{\sqrt V} = 1.227\times10^{-2} \Rightarrow \sqrt V = 100 \Rightarrow V = 10^4\) V.

questions.q: Taking into account of the significant figures, what is the value of 9.99 m − 0.0099 m?
questions.sol: \(9.99 - 0.0099 = 9.9801\). In subtraction keep the fewest decimal places (two, from 9.99): 9.98 m.

questions.q: A screw gauge has least count of 0.01 mm and there are 50 divisions in its circular scale. The pitch of the screw gauge is:
questions.sol: Least count \(= \dfrac{\text{pitch}}{\text{divisions}}\): pitch \(= 0.01\times50 = 0.5\) mm.

questions.q: The phase difference between displacement and acceleration of a particle in a simple harmonic motion is:
questions.sol: In SHM \(a = -\omega^2x\): acceleration is always opposite to displacement, a phase difference of \(\pi\) rad.
